title: ***Mild spoilers, but won't ruin the movie for anyone who would've enjoyed it***
review:
Samuel L. Jackson is the only reason this movie doesn't bore you to death. He completely carries the film, which takes at least 45 minutes to captivate interest. When Fury's not speaking or figuring things out in real time it is a massive cringefest that failed to avoid creating plot holes due to it being set in 1995. Captain Marvel herself seems to exist solely as a deus ex machina to defeat Thanos in Endgame, and those telling you that Brie Larson has "presence" should actually be telling you that she just has a massive chip on her shoulder for some reason. The only other MCU character who comes close in that regard is Dr. Strange, but remember he had his entire career and skillset that he felt defined him taken from him permanently. Carol Danvers seems pissed that the raw energy beams she can emit at will from her hands, making her one of the most powerful people in the universe, are something she has to work to control. The plot holes: In the first Avengers movie in 2012, we're told that Nick Fury started experimenting with the Tesseract to create advanced weaponry due to Thor's arrival to New Mexico in 2011. Fury even went so far as to say that this event informed us that we weren't alone in the universe. Now we're told that Fury had the Tesseract 17 years earlier and at that same time bore witness to three alien warships who launched advanced alien weaponry at the North American continent, which would have killed millions if not for Captain Marvel. Apparently that wasn't enough of a wake up call. Also, we're led to believe that the following events did not qualify as an "emergency" to Nick Fury worthy of calling for Captain Marvel's help: Thor fighting a sentinel from Asgard in New Mexico, Hawkeye shooting Nick Fury and Loki taking the Tesseract before opening a portal and invading earth with an alien army, the Mandarin escalating attacks on US soil up to the point hat he kidnapped the President of the United States, Malekith landing a spaceship in London and using the Aether to attempt to enslave humanity, Hydra attempting to assassinate Fury leading to him faking his own death so that he can keep them from activating Project Insight which would kill tens/hundreds of millions, Dormammu almost swallowing Earth, and Ultron almost raising Sokovia high enough in the atmosphere to create an extinction level event. When Captain Marvel gets a rundown of the last 8 years she's going to be pissed at Fury for not activating that pager she gave him in 1995 about a dozen different times.

Predictability: No one who's watched Agents of SHIELD fell for the plot twist. I doubt anyone who watched Guardians of the Galaxy did either. In fact, they gave the audience a massive hint about 10 minutes in. That made the long, slow buildup to it that lasted an hour worthless. In it we basically see repeated montages of a strong female pilot persevering through sexist jokes (the same "cockpit" joke is repeated twice in this film), learn about a brave a single mother, and wonder about a brilliant female doctor until we're presented with a cringey farmhouse speech. Based on the marketing and Brie Larson's plethora of comments about the film, if any of this surprises anyone I bet they are also shocked when jack comes out of the box.

Vomitus Maximus: We're led to believe at the crescendo of all drama in the film that Captain Marvel is presented with an ultimatum of great import - she will just have to be only a human. If you recall, Peter Quill faced the same dilemma, but in order to do so he gave up the god-like power of a Celestial. Captain Marvel, on the other hand, becomes more powerful in doing so. What a sacrifice...

SJWisms: Yes, there are many. Who cares. Off-hand digs at famous Trump comments, a script that seems to plagiarize a Pelosi speech for its dialogue at times, etc. A film can overcome all that if it's entertaining. This movie wasn't. The verdict: You will get out of this film what you want. If you are a dedicated MCU fan, especially one who's watched the associated TV series, you will be annoyed at the awkwardness this film creates by going back in time and crapping on key plot points of the previous films. On the other hand if you think the wage gap is real or better yet think that the fantastical fiction of an elderly white man could possibly affect that in any positive way, this will be your cup of tea. Therefore, don't assume the poor ratings are trolls, and don't assume the good ones are bots paid for by the studio. People really are this far apart on issues of all kinds in 2019, and the popular reception of Captain Marvel will reflect that. As for me personally, only The Incredible Hulk (2008) was worse and I really wish the MCU would've invested the energy they put into this film into a standalone Black Widow one. She's a much more developed character played by the right actress and she relies on her wits and skills, not energy beams, to succeed. And they still could've checked their SJW boxes and we all could've just ignored them in peace.

title: Serves its purpose within the grand MCU tapestry

Nicely done. > Ben Mendelsohn: I'm sure he's a great actor, but the recent roles he's had in high profile franchises have been very one dimensional. This one has a little more nuance for him to shine. New perspective on his range. > Music: I get that we're going for the 90s nostalgia factor + a skew towards the social highlights, but the music felt a little forced. In contrast to GoG, where the music blended effortlessly; here it was noticed ... and when it's noticed, it's a low grade distraction. > Coulson's instincts: sure we can peer into the future, but for the purposes of this film, there should have been an establishing scene between Coulson and Fury to justify the stairwell scene. Otherwise, the retro-justification just felt fuzzy. > Yon-Rogg's last stand: played for a laugh, but this bit could have been more impactful/less predictable if there was more upfront establishing the prove-yourself-to-me theme AND Jude Law didn't play it so exaggerated, which was basically shouting "blast me"

Overall, enjoyable. Necessary connecting film. But now that we've got "First Avenger" out of the way, the true test is with the "Winter Solder" chapter.

title: Bittersweet
review:
I am coming forward with my first review on IMDB, because I have noticed a lot of backlash and friction that this movie has led to. I think it is unfortunate that it has led to a point where our opinions and words are questioned, because in the end the purpose of reviews is to push producers and directors to be more original and creative in their work, but that is different discussion.

I will provide my take on the movie "Captain Marvel" and this is my opinion. Please understand that I have watched all the Marvel Movies, and was a comic book fanatic when I was a kid, so every comic book adaptation that I plan on watching gives me nothing, but excitement. Unfortunately, this movie ended up flat, with potential that wasn't reached. I was utterly surprised because Marvel has released endless entertainment, because the focus has always been on what the fans wanted to see. I will focus on three things for my review: Direction, Action, and Brie Larson.

Direction: I will honestly admit that I didn't follow "Captain Marvel" as much and wanted to understand that character's story when I came in to watch this movie. The whole entire journey felt rushed and forced to me. It was nothing but good and cute moments in spurts that provided no direction whatsoever. Thor's first movie provided a simple journey of a man that had a lesson to learn to become a good leader with the weakness of arrogance. I was expecting something similar with this movie, but the movie didn't provide that. I had to ask my friends after watching this movie on what this is about? I honestly would have liked the movie to focus a lot on her to present us journey of her discovering herself, but it was filled with short discussions between characters which felt like a TV series from CW. I think the directors wanted to provide a sophisticated origin story that sets up the character for the upcoming "End Game", but it honestly ended up me questioning if this movie was necessary.

Action: The special effects was wonderful, I honestly can't say enough about what they did with Samuel Jackson. He really looked young and it was hard to tell. Being a big fan of him and loving his work like "Pulp Fiction" it brought me a smile. The action sequence was bittersweet. I honestly didn't enjoy the lighting and how it was presented. It felt like watching Michael Bay's Transformer action scene in the dark, and I it was frustrating. The space battle scene was a good way to end it, but it was an attempted recovery that felt flat at that point.

Brie Larson: I am not questioning her ability to act, but I felt that this was not the right character for her to play, and I am not saying that she should be cut from being Captain Marvel. I don't know if it was her or the director not giving her enough to work with. I enjoy watching character's develop in a story and that being presented because it is a journey that we are taking with the character, but I felt that she wasn't able to do that. There were action scenes, the tone of her voice, and her posture in which led me to cringe because it felt forced. All this leads me to also question the director of the movie.

Conclusion: "Captain Marvel" ended up being the weakest movie in the Marvel Universe due to lack of developing the main protagonist. She didn't face any major dilemma or problem. Also the structure felt forced and difficult to understand what direction the movie was trying to make. Unfortunately the movie ended up making Goose the Cat the most intriguing character which is I am sure not the way they wanted. I would like to see a new direction for Captain Marvel so we can love her character because I want to as well. One suggestion that I would like to make for the Russo Brothers and Marvel is to integrate her in the Guardians of the Galaxy movie because in the comics her story provides a lot more intrigue.

title: Captain Marvel soars well enough but still can't land perfectly.
review:
Marvel's newest movie starring their first superhero is a winner that soars thanks to a strong leading performance by Brie Larson and a twisty take on the ever tiresome origin story.

Taking inspiration from 90s science fiction thrillers like Men in Black, Species, and a little visual flair from the likes of ID4 and The Fifth Element, the action moves from planet to planet as the half human/half alien soldier Carol Danvers goes on avital mission to thwart a sinister extraterrestrial race.

Carol Danvers (Larson) is an elite member of the special forces overseen by the powerful Kree empire who are locked in battle with the shapeshifting aliens known as the Skrulls. Unfortunately, she is plagued by nightmares suggesting a past life on Earth so she teams up with the human secret agent Nick Fury (SLJ) to uncover her forgotten memories and prevent her home planet's war from spreading to Earth.

The space battles and chase scenes are energetic and fun to watch. Brie Larson is likable and snarky as Carol Danvers, often delivering one-liners with a sly quip and a smirk. Jackson is much more comedic as Nick Fury in this film, but displays a resourceful streak when called for. Ben Mendelsohn often steals the scene as the Skrull general Talos. Some of the most heartfelt and dramatic moments come from his character suprisingly enough.

The film is not perfect however and it mostly comes down to other supporting characters getting shortchanged. There is a very small cameo appearance by Ronan the Accuser (Lee Pace) who is built up as a major threat but then shortly disappears. In the first two acts of the film, Danvers has a whole team of Kree warriors who are given little development aside from the stock characterization: Big guy; black guy; the chick; you get the idea. Clark Gregg reappears as Agent Coulson but doesn't do much (aside from resembling a young Dennis Quaid).

On the other hand, this avoids the film being bogged down in subplots and does make the movie more fast paced. What is most interesting about the plot is the introduction of some moral ambiguity to the MCU regarding ethics of war and espionage and military secrets. Not quite as well as The Winter Soldier and you wish they went further in that direction.

However, CAPTAIN MARVEL remains another solid entry to the ever expanding MCU thanks to Brie Larson's charming performance, a fun buddy/mystery storyline, and yes, an enticing tease for the upcoming mega-blockbuster AVENGERS: ENDGAME.

title: Yeah!! Definitely a nice surprise !!
review:
To be honest I don't think I watch a trailer for this film before seeing it, which is rare. Most films that you want to see is because you saw a trailer for it but this one I took a chance and just watch it without any preconceived notions. However I'll be fully honest I have become more and more disinterested with the MCU or comic book films in general over the past couple of years, comic book film fatigue/over saturation has taken its toll on me. So with that In mind I was pleasantly surprised by this film, overall it was a really entertaining watch from start to finish and gave us something fresh in the MCU.

There are many positives to the film firstly the directing is strong throughout and definitely has its own style whilst still feeling like a film within the MCU. Anna Boden and Ryan Fleck have done a good job with this film. Not much else to say because there was nothing mind blowing from a directing standpoint but very solid throughout.

The cast is probably the strongest part of the film and the performances that are given throughout. Firstly Brie Larson as Carol Danvers..............yeah she is good. Does a good job handling the varied situations that the character faces and twists and turns that present themselves as the film goes along. Even though when you meet the character she is far removed from Earth you immediately gravitated to her because of her charm/personality its weirdly infections. Eventually when the film moves onto activity on Earth thats when Larson really settles down into the role and makes it her own, along side one of the all time greats.

That all time great I'm referencing is obviously Samuel L. Jackson who is terrible.........................nah of course he is great in the film, showing us a new angle to the character of Nick Fury. The man is a legend and can do no wrong.

Other mentions should definitely be Jude Law and Ben Mendelsohn who are both great is there respective roles. Its nice actually how they are presented in the film at first is turned 180 degrees the other way in the end. Even though I must say that I saw it a mile off............its was still a nice twist that worked well with the story and the character of Carol Danvers and how she becomes Captain Marvel.

(Also Goose, such a cute "cat" that was involved in some of the highlights of the film).

Last positive has to be the special effects in the film, the action scenes are incredibly shot and have some great effects in them. I suppose the best effects have to be with the "de-ageing" of Samuel L. Jackson, which are superb throughout. You know when a special effect has done its job when you completely forget about it once you've seen it once. As soon as your introduced to Nick Fury the first time, its a pleasant shock but after that I forgot about it. Shows how seamless and fantastic the effects were.

Overall this film is 75% out of 100 or 7.5 out of 10 it surprised the hell out of me and I really enjoyed it even though I wasn't bothered about seeing it before hand. Also the fact that I'm not a MCU fan or even a comic book film fan anymore it was a fun ride. A really pleasant watch from start to finish with some great acting, interesting story and some fantastic special effects.........what could you want more in a MCU film??

(Quick side note another positive I've remembered is the fact that there is not that much of the dreaded MCU humour in this film. There is some humour here and there but its not overused, some of it even made me laugh and I cant remember the last time I actually laughed with a MCU film instead of laughing at a MCU film).

title: Much better than expected, and the problems weren't what I thought they'd be
review:
I'll admit to not being excited about this movie. But it won't be the first time I've not expected to like a Marvel movie and been proved wrong... and this is no exception. I came out of the theatre feeling as though, by and large, I enjoyed what I'd seen. Contrary to expectations, this film didn't put an agenda over story... thought that's not to say the agenda didn't rear its ugly head once or twice... or ten or fifteen times.

The thing holding me back from loving this movie however is the real problem, the character arc of Captain Marvel.

All good/satisfying character arcs can be broken down to three essential ingredients that need to be explored throughout the course of the story:

1 - A challenge that is beyond the character's current ability level 2 - The journey that character must go through to EARN (I can't stress this word enough) the necessary skills, knowledge and experience to overcome that challenge 3 - A conclusion where the character shows the hard won results of step 2 to either overcome the challenge, or at the least put in a damn close effort that is far beyond what the character could have done in step 1.

Captain Marvel had the first ingredient well and truly covered. The movie starts with Carol Danvers needing to overcome memory loss, not knowing how to use her powers, and needing to find the necessary strength to overcome what will eventually stand in her way. So far so good.

The problem comes with the next step which is the most important as without it the third ingredient will never work. The journey she went through to get from step 1 to 3 continually gave her what she needed rather than make her earn it. There are flash backs to struggles that happened before the main narrative, but you never see Carol go through try fail cycles or struggle as all good characters do in order to grow. Instead she just moves through the story and lets the plot simply lavish gifts upon her to overcome the problems from step one.

The frustrating thing is that this could have been fixed with just a few scenes. Show her struggling to control her powers, let her fail a few times with disastrous results, show us the cost of not overcoming her problems that drives her to fight harder. Tony Stark struggled in a cave under gunpoint with a serious injury and no resources, then had to take a hard look at his life and his legacy and overcome that along with some serious mental trauma before finally we had Iron Man, and that was why that character works.

Carol Danvers is competent at the start and only gets stronger as and when the story needs her too which makes it impossible to create stakes and give us viewers a character to get behind.

Other than that this movie was actually pretty good. The supporting cast was great, the concept pretty solid, the CGI out of this world, and despite a few cringeworthy retcons, it works within the larger MCU.

So overall, it wasn't the politics or Brie Larson's off screen comments that loses the stars from this review, but fundamental storytelling. Oh, and one other thing...

Even if you're trying to make a light hearted movie and having fun, your superhero should never bee whooping in excitement and joy as they kill people. By this I don't mean cheering in success at surviving the day or winning a battle, I mean the whoops of fun that might associated with a child playing. Seeing Captain Marvel do it as she destroys countless spaceships and takes countless lives took me right out of the movie.

Overall, this was pretty good and worth a watch, but there's definitely room for improvement.

title: Disappointed, but still enjoyable
review:
Oh boy Captain Marvel. You left me enjoyed having watched a decent film, but waiting for the ORIGINAL Captain Marvel film (The Shazam movie, coming out in April) more than wanting to see this again.

This is an interesting film. It's a film I don't hate, but don't feel emotionally compelled towards it. So here we are, talking about my opinions on Captain Marvel. Oh and spoilers are here as well, you have been warned.

Let's start with the opening, which instead of the Marvel logo showing scenes from all the films, instead shows scenes of ALL of Stan Lee's cameos in the MCU, before ending with 'Thank You Stan'. That was such a great opening for me, but that was the most emotional I felt in the film. And yes, Stan Lee has a cameo. And it's quite meta and funny.

Moving on the main character herself: Captain Marvel, played by Brie Larson. She does a good job acting, which is nice, but sadly I feel Brie Larson's talent are undermined by the fact Captain Marvel is kind of a boring character. She's too strong, in my opinion, and yes whilst the MCU has powerful characters like Thor and Hulk, the way they implement them into the films they're in works. And those two characters mentioned get better with each film, so I'm hoping that's the same with Captain Marvel, because it would be a waste of Brie Larson's acting abilities.

As for the supporting cast, it's all right I guess. The best supporting character is Samuel L Jackson's Nick Fury, who is very funny in the film's buddycop comedy section. Which doesn't last very long until it's replaced by another thing, but I'll get to plotting later. I know people hate when Hollywood uses CGI or de-aging techniques for films, but I liked the de-aging used for Samuel L Jackson. He's not the badass we've seen. Captain Marvel is the first superhero he meets and it's alright to show naivety. Scratch that, the cat is the best character. It's a great comic relief and really funny how the two interact. Oh and the cat makes Nick Fury lose an eye. Told you there were spoilers. The other good supporting character is Lashana Lynch's Maria Rambeau. She's a interesting character and her relationship with Captain Marvel/Carol Danvers is nice. If she turned out to be gay, I would be fine. Representation is very important nowadays and it would be nice to show it instead of SAYING THAT A CHARACTER IS SOMETHING WITHOUT SHOWING IT (I'm looking at you Solo: A Star Wars Story)

The problems with the film are weird. The visual effects are pretty bland, especially from Marvel movies that have had amazing visual effects. There wasn't really any exciting action scenes, except for the one towards the end when Captain Marvel uses her powers for the first time. However, the biggest problem for me is the story. At first, it's Ben Mendelsohn who's meant to be the bad guy, and honestly I would be fine with that. In this movie, he is a compelling character who I like, similar to how I like him as Nolan Sorrento in Ready Player One. But no, instead we get a twist villain. Because Disney sure realised that their track record with these characters needed a redemption. So instead, Jude Law turns out to be the villain. Considering Disney owns 20th Century Fox, I'm now expecting Jude Law's Dumbledore to be evil in the next Fantastic Beasts (joking). The problem isn't the twist, it's surprising and interesting, but it's that the character himself has no motivations about being evil, other than being in a war with the opposing species. And yea, Jude Law's character might be the worst villain since Malekirth in the MCU. Yeah, I'm serious.

Before I finish I want to quickly compare this to two other groundbreaking films: Black Panther and Wonder Woman. For Black Panther, it's because there is a GoFundMe page to get girls to see Captain Marvel, similar to how there was a GoFundMe page to get black people to see Black Panther. The problem is whilst this film is important and will have a cultural impact, it's not as good as Black Panther. For Wonder Woman, that was a much better film because it didn't need to show scenes of men treating women like nothing like this film did sometimes. It wanted to be a great film, and it did, and that's why it's the best film in the DCEU. Captain Marvel feels like it's in the bottom half.

As I watched, I noticed despite being a female superhero film, there were very few women or girls at the cinema. This isn't a complaint, I'm just pointing something out. I'm not detracting anyone from seeing this film. If you want to, go ahead. If a girl gets inspired from this film, that's great. I'm not here to be an arse. I'm just here to say, whilst a good film, Captain Marvel is one of the weaker MCU films and certainly not as great as Wonder Woman.

title: As a Marvel fan, I'm truly dissatisfied
review:
I was not hyped for this film at all whatsoever but I knew it was coming and as a huge marvel fan, I wouldn't want to miss any films. I knew this was just an origin film and nothing special.

I expected some action and I got some, I expected Coulson and got him but very little of him, it seems that they just threw him in there just to show he was around at the time, he really wasn't utilized at all by the film. Fury was surprisingly much more comedic than any of his marvel films which was somewhat amusing, because it wasn't like Fury knew about heroes or intergalactic threats so this was all new to him. However I thought it was extremely ridiculous how he really lost his eye...by a stupid cat, like really? C'mon they could have done so much better. He didn't even have much of a reaction either, he kind of just let it go like "oh well, there goes my eye",obviously he didn't say that. I was expecting something else to happen since he said that one line in Captain America: Winter Soldier, "the last time I trusted someone, I lost an eye" making it seem like it was someone's fault, I expected him to lose in somewhat of the same way thor lost his eye in Ragnarok, he'd be in a fight or something and someone would get a cheap shot on him by hacking his eye out and it'd be all dramatic, I would have loved that but it seems marvel is too scared to make it dark since its not infinity war or endgame, which are the two most known films with somewhat dark tones.

To know that Brie Larson is an academy award winner and playing Captain Marvel, in who I had very little knowledge of her backstory, is a bit disappointing because she was so straight-faced throughout the film. Even when she cracked jokes, not only were they forced but it seemed hard for her to crack a smile, there were only a couple times in which she actually smiled and you were able to see the lines on her face as proof. But performance as whole was a bit disappointing, she just wasn't very animated.

Captain marvel's backstory overall wasn't that interesting and at times I felt very bored, even as the huge marvel geek fan I am. I always get chills and am in awe when a hero has their moment in a film to embrace who they really are or that special scene with their own score playing in the background, maybe even a good line to go along with it. Heroes that I originally had no interest in like Doctor Strange, Black Panther, etc. Had that special moment and redeemed themselves as characters filled in through actors who actually fulfilled the characters' intentions and persona. And I'm not just saying this because she is a female protagonist, I ain't biased either because there are good woman-lead roles such as Alita or Wonder Woman that were successful. Those that want to praise every marvel film or maybe just the fact that this one has Brie Larson, is just trolling or trying to boost for marvel, I know it sounds like its just my opinion but its heavily agreed on by the majority of people who saw it.

Finally the CGI. It was as good as most marvel films. In the end however when Marvel was soaring through the sky bashing through those alien missiles coming to earth, the effects on her face looked straight up like black panther's end fight scene, horrible, definitely IN the uncanny Valley.

The end credits scene of Endgame was perfect, probably better than the film itself. This definitely wasn't a film that I'd recommend. Just a basic backstory. It was meh.

title: Good story, bad character design
review:
Marvel was overdue for it's first female lead film, and Captain Marvel seeked to establish Carol Danvers as one of the main faces of the next generation of heroes, expected to take the spotlight after characters like Tony Stark, Steve Rogers, and Bruce Banner either die or retire after the upcoming Endgame.

Unfortunately, I believe that the filmmakers let the responsibility of establishing MCU's first lead female hero influence Carol's character design far too much. The film overstates her power in exchange for good character development and personality, resulting in her over-powered nature. The film lacks times where Carol seems to truly be in danger of losing, which is a vital element to good superhero movies. Her ability to destroy missiles and ships simply by flying through them makes her far too powerful to make for a good character. It truly seems as though Thanos will not stand a chance against Danvers, which is absurd considering her power is only from being exposed to one Infinity Stone, while his is from wielding all six Stones.

The film does have its strengths however, particularly in its storyline, which is refreshing, as finally an ugly shapeshifting alien race is the good guy this time. Fury and Coulson are perfectly de-aged by the use of CGI, and they make the movie much more enjoyable. The action and effects are good as usual, redeeming the movie as being alright.

And now im just left disappointed and annoyed that this emotionless robotic hero is going to sweep in an beat Thanos.

TL;DR: I feel like people were too focused on making Danvers a "strong woman" to give her any depth or emotion which resulted in super hero who is downright forgettable.

title: Can one poor performance ruin a movie?
review:
6. That's how many stars out of 10 I give this movie, and honestly I think I'm being very generous. Breaking down the movie into parts, I'd give effects (C.G.I., etc at good 9, maybe 10! The work on de-aging Sam Jackson's character, Nick Fury, was so good, it was almost hard to believe. The other effects, I.e. explosions, particle beams, whatever, all look good too. The overall story I'd give a 7, maybe 8. Decent, but while they included a couple surprises, they weren't that surprising. The acting? Well, almost all the actors were between good and really good. Only a couple were just o.k. and only one was not very good at all. The problem is, the actor that was the worse, was the lead, Brie Larson. Her performance would have been spot on, had she been playing a cyborg, with no feelings or expressions. Most of her acting was somewhere between a grimace, or smirk. She had those two expressions down pat! Beyond that however, I couldn't tell if she was happy, sad, angry, scared, or just constipated. A poor performance by the lead is tough for any film to recover from, and this one for me just couldn't. On a bright note, my popcorn was good!

The above is just my opinion. Your mileage could vary.

title: Definitely not the best or "first" Female Super Hero!
review:
Looking at this movie objectively, I can easily say it's not a terrible movie but also not a great movie either.

The effects where average and excelled at making Samuel L. Jackson's Nick Fury look amazing. Sadly, Brie Larson as Captain Marvel gave an average to underwhelming performance leaving a dull impression. It was clear she didn't have the ability to carry the movie on her own and needed supporting actors to even make it work.

Unfortunately the story didn't adhere to the pre-established lore in the comics and in fact dangerously deviates and changes one of the best villain races in the MCU. And ends up leaving Ronan the Accuser probably one the cool'est villains in Marvel Movies thus far, feels underused and improperly implemented story wise.

If you were hoping for a great answer to the anticipated question as to how Nick Fury lost his eye. Sadly it's probably the most disappointing aspect of the movie with little to no imagination in the execution.

All said and done, due to the points stated as well as poor writing and directing. Also considering the history of the Marvel Cinematic Universe this movie is slightly below average and a generally forgettable but somewhat enjoyable film.

title: Definitely disappointing.
review:
Warning: Heavy Spoilers ahead

Pros: -Great supporting cast, especially Ben Mendelsohn

-Gorgeous CGI and Visual Effects

-Some fun 90's nostalgia

Cons: -Brie Larson's acting of Captain Marvel. The whole movie she feels condescending, arrogant, and very unlikable. Felt like she had never bothered to pick up a comic book and read what the character was actually like. And while some other characters started that way, Iron Man and Doctor Strange for example, RDJ and Benedict Cumberbatch played them with enough charisma and charm that they were likable, and when their characters dynamically changed at the end, the audience actually cared. Captain Marvel was exactly the same from start to finish, and since she wasn't interesting or enjoyable at the start, that's a problem. I don't know if that's a fault of the writing or her acting, but she felt wooden and uninteresting the whole movie.

-Her powers were largely unexplained. She gets hit by an energy core and somehow absorbs it. Why? Can all humans do that? How come she could, and what exactly does that mean? Obviously comics fans will know the extent and ability of her powers, but since this film kept changing all their characters from the source material, they should have explained what MCU Carol can do.

-Fight scene choreography was very choppily edited. Almost at Bourne Identity levels for some parts. It was kind of distracting, and detracted from what could have been cool scenes.

-Captain Mar-Vell was a Kree warrior that mentored her in the comics. Carol took the name from him after he was killed. He was an essential character that had existed for a long time, and the movie instead made him an old woman, and then killed her off after a few minutes of screentime.

-The Skrulls weren't good guys in the comics. They attacked first, and since their introduction in 1962, they've been a force for evil, who's goal is death and destruction of key individuals in order to assume control of entire planets. They were not poor refugees unjustly being hunted by the Kree. This movie kept rewriting characters, and it didn't really pay off. Now the Secret Invasion storyline that many fans were hoping for probably won't happen.

-It felt like there were absolutely no stakes in this movie. Captain Marvel never appeared to struggle with anything, ever. She laughs off people hitting her, effortlessly destroys all the bombs in the end, has no problem piloting unknown aircraft,etc. I know that's not uncommon for superhero films, but she never appeared hurt, never got confused, never showed any kind of weakness whatsoever, and that makes me uncertain about what she'll be like in Endgame. There never felt like there was any danger to her, the Earth, or anyone around her. Even when the Kree fired a bunch of nukes at Earth, it never felt like anything bad could happen.

-Climax of the movie happened in like 30 seconds. Kree show up, launch a few missiles, CM flies up, pushes one missile into the others (conveniently all of them blow up at the same time), CM flies to the Kree ship and tells them to leave, and they're like "okay, bye." End final battle.

-Kind of a nitpick, but why doesn't Carol's jacket burn up at the end when shes leaving the atmosphere, or her body is on fire while flying? We've seen she can melt metal with her powers, but her leather jacket is just indistructable I guess.

-Also a nitpick, the little girl telling her mom to go on a suicide mission to set a good example for her felt kind of weird.

-Unexplained mastery over her powers. Somehow she regains her powers after having them "taken away" by the Supreme Intelligence (which was probably just a power dampening device), but after she removes it, she effortlessly uses all the new power with no problem. There's a moment where she just decides that she can fly, with no prior inclination or hint that that's possible. Shes falling, then closes her eyes, smiles, and starts flying, as if somehow she knew all along that she could, and decided that she didn't want to up until this point. Also, somehow she can fly around and breathe in space with no real explanation (despite her not being Binary). Movie did not do a good job of explaining her powers to the audience, or what she could do.

-The Avengers twist at the end. You've got to be kidding me. The Avengers didn't get their name from a nickname painted on Carol's plane wing.

-Nick Fury losing his eye to Goose. Again, it feels like they were ret-conning the whole MCU for a cheap laugh or to somehow make us care more about this movie.

-End credit scene was probably a clip from Endgame, so there wasn't really any point to staying for it. Second end credit scene added nothing, and wasn't even really funny.

-Most of the jokes in here didn't land with me. There were definitely some funny ones (mostly the ones from Ben Mendelsohn), but a lot of them I knew it was a joke, but didn't find it humorous.

-Movie was extremely predictable (more so than a typical Marvel movie). Aside from the Tesseract showing up, I knew what was going to happen 10 minutes before it did. The film was also really boring for a lot of it, which I was surprised by.

I really, really wanted to like this film, but I cant give it better than a 5/10

title: Certainly not the worst, but not the best either, just very average
review:
This film was...okay. Watched it with a friend, we share the same opinion on it, it certainly isn't bad. It has bad aspects that can ruin parts of the film, but overall, it's okay, watchable and tolerable. I have some issues with it and I will address the negatives first and then the positives.

Negatives:
  • The child acting is awful, and given how much time is spent in that barn, the really bad child acting takes away from the importance of the scene, and makes it drag whenever she's in it, even the Skrull kid, even though she barely says anything, her facial expressions are so unnatural and don't match the tone.
  • At some points, the CGI could be overdone, basically it made the visuals unconvincing and distracting. Although the visual effects on Nick Fury are good, the same can't be said for Agent Coulson, his eyes looks weird, it had the same problem as Rogue One where at times the CGI made the expressions unnatural. There is one scene where Carol is falling from a great height, and as she nears the ground it does a close up of her, the CGI looked weird to me and put me off.
  • Some of the twists that were made came way too quick, namely when you realise Fury's boss and Coulson is a Skrull at the start. This links in with the next issue
  • For some characters the development is lacking, especially Keller, we knew nothing about him prior to his Skrull reveal, so we just got introduced to him as a Skrull, but I can forgive that because Talos is developed very well. But where the character development is most lacking is the Starforce Team. Possible one of the most crucial areas to develop, and it's just missing. Jude Law's character (forgot his name) is developed somewhat, and you care enough about him, but the others, I can't remember any of their names, given how their significance to Carol's story is just undermined. Their fight scene at the end doesn't make you care enough, due to their lack of development, the whole team is just Sam Rockwell's character from Galaxy Quest.
  • The use of Come As You Are is strange, the title of the song fits the context of the scene perfectly, but it goes on for too long, and from the get go the actual tune doesn't match the scene, it should finish earlier, or at least fade out quicker, but it carries onto a smaller fight scene and doesn't match what's happening on the screen/
  • At some points Brie Larson's acting was a bit bland but that didn't bother me, it was more just to do with the flat delivery of her cheesy line, but to be fair cheesy lines are just what Marvel like to do.
  • There was some bad sound effects in the training scene at the start. The punches sound awful and incredibly tame, still trying to figure out if it's sound editing or mixing.
  • Opening scene is a bit dull and boring, and slow. Just let it slide and enjoy the rest of the film


Positives:
  • I mentioned Brie Larson's acting being bland at times, but that's a very small portion of the film, overall she is very good, she brings a natural charisma to the role and it works perfectly, reminds me a lot of her role in Scott Pilgrim vs The World. She is brilliant as Carol Denvers and after seeing her play the role I doubt anyone else could've done it better.
  • I've seen people complain about a feminist agenda, quite frankly I just think it's stupid, it's not like Doctor Who season 11.
  • Samuel L Jackson, as always, is amazing as Nick Fury, the effects to make him look younger work very well, his hair looks a bit weird but his mannerisms look natural as does his facial expressions.
  • Jude Law is alright, really he's just another forgettable character (villain?), his performance is actually good as is his acting, his chemistry with Brie is good as well.
  • The action sequences, bar a few, are pretty good, especially the one on the train.
  • The reveal that the Skrull were actually innocent and looking for a home worked for me, and the Kree being the enemy (although we already knew the Kree were bad from Guardians of the Galaxy) worked for me, also, finding out they were Kree already gave you some doubt to begin with, but the Skrull gave you doubts as well, and when Carol finds out she's been on the wrong side, it develops her character further.
  • At first the Carol Denvers/Vers thing confused me, but then they gave me a very satisfying explanation, which is one thing about the film, if you're confused about something it gives you a satisfying explanation and leaves you with answers and no questions.
  • I liked Goose the Cat, just saying, thought Goose was pretty cool
  • The pacing, except the first few minutes, is pretty good. Everything moves at a good pace, it doesn't linger anywhere for too long, it transitions to new places appropriately, the flashbacks aren't unnecessary and are actually important to see, as we find out information the same times she does.


Overall, it's a pretty average film, my original rating was a 7 because an 8 felt too nice for the film given its flaws, then when I evaluated how much the positives outweigh the negatives, and how much the negatives take away from the film, my rating dropped to a 6, which doesn't make it bad, just average. I feel like it's somewhere between Iron Man 3 and Captain America: The First Avenger. It's not bad, not amazing, just average. It's a fun enough film and I don't regret watching it

title: Captain Vanilla and the Attack of the Underwhelming Finished Product
review:
Never written a review before, but this film made me feel like I had to. I wasn't sure what it was going to deliver when I went to see it, no one could have failed to be aware of the controversy surrounding it, or the media's frenzied over hyping of it, which they took to ridiculous levels. But I'm an MCU fan and I wanted to give this film a fair go, I just wanted another good entry into the franchise. But I've got to say what I got was, at best, a bottom of the league average film.

The story line is nothing special, it's an origin story, and they always stick to the same formula, it's the performances that sell it and get you involved. As always Samuel L. Jackson extremely watchable, when is he not, he is the coolest guy on the face of the planet. A lot of other people have been praising Ben Mendelsohn as Talos, and I'm not going to break with that, he is first rate and manages to steal the film off of everyone. Not a particular Jude Law fan, but he is capable of great performances, he is okay in this, does enough to make his character work, but that's all. I have to praise Lashana Lynch though, there is very little to her character, but she certainly knows how to make a little go a long way, some actresses would have struggled to bring this character to life, but she manages to do it with ease and style. I had never heard of her before this film, but I will be looking out for her in the future, and I can't wait to see her in something that will really allow her to show off her acting skills. Now we come to Brie Larson, and here is where the problems start. She gives a one note, monotone performance, and goes through the entire film, when she is not being arrogant and snarky, looking bored out of her skull. It is a well worn phrase, but in this case it really does describe perfectly her performance, she just phones it in, there is nothing to her character, be it Carol Danvers or Captain Marvel, she is totally flat in both. She displays no charm, charisma or warmth, she doesn't connect with the audience on any level, even the most undeveloped characters in the MCU, such as Hawkeye, connect with the viewer. He is the family man, he provides the soul, from Larson you get nothing, you don't like her, you don't dislike her, she is just there. When her character discovers she can fly, there is nothing from her, no emotional reaction, no surprise, shock or even a smile, nothing. How am I supposed to connect, to or with, a character that seems totally detached from everything around her, and lacks anything that could be described as a personality.

If you are thinking, or hoping, that maybe the action sequences will save the day, that Captain Marvel will serve up something special, sorry to say you are out of luck. They are up to the usual standard of a Marvel film, they are what you would expect, and that's the problem, you expect it. There is no great emotional impact from any of it, and there is no humor, Brie Larson doesn't sell it at all, she never seems to struggle to beat anyone, never appears to be in any danger. The end battle was a prime example of this, I was bored, I don't enjoy watching a character who never struggles, who never has to earn anything, who can do everything and is so over powered it's untrue. If the outcome is never in any doubt, or there is no journey to get to the outcome, what is the point of watching. Also this is Marvel's first prequel, and I hate prequels, because they always manage to screw up continuity, mess up the timeline and devalue the films that have gone before. Ronan the Accuser, the big bad from Guardians of the Galaxy, is shown to be nothing more than a wimp in this one, he runs away from Captain Marvel, not kidding, he flees from her. It took all the Guardians had to bring him down, how weak are they that they could only just defeat someone who ran away from Marvel, this undercuts Guardians of the Galaxy completely, and tarnishes that film. The worst offense though has to be how this film retcons that whole speech from Nick Fury to Captain America about losing his eye in Winter Soldier, he loses his eye in this film because the damn cat scratched him, that's it, a cat scratch. Don't try and sell me on that whole 'He said he was going to trust the cat' drivel, it just doesn't fit in, it just disrespects Fury's character and the whole franchise. This brings us to the biggest problem going forward this film could pose to the whole MCU starting with EndGame. It has established Captain Marvel as being way over powered, Superman like if you will, and characters like this lead to one conclusion, which I call the Justice League Trap. Now JL wasn't a particularly good film, but it had Batman, Aquaman, Wonder Woman, Flash and Cyborg going head to head with the villain, and they couldn't bring him down, they needed Superman to turn up and save the day, which he did. Something which poses the question going forward 'Why do you need them if you have Superman ?' They are all redundant and unnecessary as long as you have Superman. If Marvel is going down that same route, which they appear to be as Kevin Feige has said Captain Marvel is the most powerful character in the MCU, what's the point of watching. All you need is Captain Marvel, every other superhero is superfluous. The Hulk, Thor, Scarlet Witch are all immensely powerful, but they are also flawed and have weaknesses, the outcome is never certain, there is doubt. With a character as OTT as Captain Marvel is being set up to be, the outcome is never in danger or doubt, she will win easily, so why watch.

I always mark films in two ways, the first part is the film itself, which I mark out of 6, and I give this one a 3, take out the problems it could cause, because we don't know, and it just about manages to be an average minus, thanks to the good level of acting from everyone other than Larson.

The remaining 4 marks come from the re-watchabilty factor. Do I want or need to see it again, will I buy it as soon as it comes out on Blu-ray or wait for it to drop in price ect. It scores zero here, there is nothing about this film that makes me want to see it again, the story is simplistic, so you get all that, there is nothing stand out about it. I have no desire to see it again in any way shape or form. Even the end credit scenes are nothing, I don't need to see Captain Plank suddenly appear again behind Black Widow (who's film this should have been), as for the one with the cat vomiting up the tesseract, well that just proves how this unnecessary and unwanted prequel just screws up continuity, in it's bid to crowbar Captain Marvel into the MCU. I knew Marvel would make a bad movie at some point, I just never thought it would be this bad, or the one before EndGame.

title: This had so much potential, and wasted it all
review:
I really hoped this movie would would be good, honestly I did. I walked into the cinema, forgot everything I heard about this movie before and hoped it would be as good as Wonder Woman. 2 hours later I walked out of the cinema and was thoroughly disappointed. Let me explain: 1. Carol Danvers felt like an emotionless robot. No wait, that is an insult to Ultron, she felt like an emotionless brick. This is NOT how I wanted to start this, (considering the current Brie Larson controversy) but it's definitely one of this movies biggest problems. I honestly don't know if it's the actor's fault or if she was just told to behave that way by whoever wrote the script, but dammit Marvel, you could have done this way better. Just look at the above mentioned Wonder woman, or Alita Battle angel. Or maybe at Valkyrie in YOUR thor ragnarok?

2. Way too much 90s nostalgia. It would have been cool in small amounts, but the 90s theme dominated the entire movie.

3. The cgi. I myself work in the computer graphics industry, and quite frankly I am tempted to kill whoever thought it was a good idea to de-age one of the lead characters for the entire movie. It's well done most of the time, but from time to time it just fails in a painfully obvious way that totally breaks immersion. Feels like a step back after the incredible job that was done to create Thanos.

4. The plot. It's like they took the Superhero 101 formula, made the hero female and then expected to create something new and engaging. Spoiler warning: they did not.

5. Some other stuff: The humor felt too forced from time to time, the pacing was all sorts of wrong in my opinion, there are some minor plotholes that jsut don't make sense. I went into far more detail in my previous reviews, but am too tired to do that again. See #7 below.

6. Marketing and Release: Let's ignore all the Brie Larson for now. But who the hell thought it was a good idea to introduce a major new character mere months before the climax they have been working towards for years? I realized after watching approximately half the movie that I would have to see Captain marvel in Endgame as a lead character. That realization made it a lot more difficult to enjoy the rest of the movie. And attempting to market a product by abusing feminism or with a dead man's Twitter account just feels wrong. I did not let this influence the my rating of this movie, but i still felt that it should be said. Shame on you, Marvel/Disney.

7. Damage control: Apparently someone decided to do some damage control when a lot of negative reviews started coming in. Sure, some of them might have been troll reviews, but as far as I can tell a good chunk of them were not. My reviews for this movie have already been removed 2 times before, and both of them were far more detailed than this one.

Having said all this I do want to also say that there also were some good things. The cat was a nice touch, as was the Stan Lee cameo. The potential for more was definitely there, but it was never really used. That's why I believe that it's a mediocre movie at best.

title: Captain Marvel will be MUCH more enjoyable if you're familiar with the 2012+ canon.
review:
I'm not one of those comic book elitists who disregards your opinion if you've forsaken the source material. In fact, I shudder to think where Marvel Comics would be if not for the life-saving injection of Marvel Studios and the resulting fan base that even includes a sect that have no interest comics. However, uniquely in the case of Captain Marvel, I feel like it's quite useful to be familiar with the Kelly Sue DeConnick canon beginning in 2012 as well as the reprisal in 2014. This comic is unabashedly feminist. Does that suck the fun out of it? No. It doesn't man-bash, but rather empowers, which is what I thought was at the heart of feminism anyway. The comic showcases a woman with an enormous native strength of will that predates the assumption of her super powers. This is accomplished without a shred of bitchiness, and is actually representative of most of the women in my life. Certainly, Carol encounters everyday obstacles exclusive to women, having been told since childhood she can't do certain things in light of her being a "girl". She doesn't always deal with these obstacles perfectly, but she also doesn't give credence to her detractors by feeling like she has to prove herself. After all, she has bigger issues to deal with...like saving the world. As a 40-something year old man, while I was acutely aware of the nuances, I never once felt like the DeConnick Captain Marvel was shoving an agenda down my throat, nor did I feel like I was reading a frilly "girl's comic". ("Not that there's anything wrong with that" in my best 90s Seinfeld).

The film quite effectively imparts this essence and bolsters it with archetypal Marvel Studios flair. After seeing the film, any reticence I may have had about Brie Larson's ability to carry this character well into future installments has been effectively obliterated. Marvel Studios continues their track record for excellent casting demonstrating insight into an actor's presence that I otherwise wouldn't have seen. I immediately accepted Larson as the de facto Carol Danvers and now would have a difficult time seeing anyone else take on the role. The chemistry between Samuel L. Jackson and Larson is real, and I love seeing these two play off each other. While I've seen several comments about the scene-steeling Goose and/or Talos, I honestly feel like that's been overstated. Captain Marvel is on the lighter side of the Marvel Studios formulaic spectrum as it's laden with humor, but its heart is undeniable. The fun 90s nostalgia is ever present, but it never becomes a crutch. The soundtrack cements the theme with such 90s standards as R.E.M., Garbage, Nirvana, and No Doubt to name a few. Additional girl-power support came out of nowhere with the inclusion of a favorite 80s Lita Ford hit. The score also does a nice job of approximating the 90s version of electronica.

We saw Captain Marvel in IMAX. The shifting aspect ratios were used sparingly but effectively, demonstrating expansive spacescapes and the overwhelming Hala skyline. While it's not the neon spectacle that was Thor Ragnarok, Captain Marvel has its share of unnaturally and richly saturated colors against deep blacks devoid of grit or grain. The dynamic soundtrack was well-balanced with excellent use of discrete directional effects and booming percussive explosions and clear dialogue.

Captain Marvel is an origin film, and while it's presumably a crucial element in the grand Marvel Cinematic Universe scheme, it will work well as a stand-alone for those who have no prior exposure to the canon. This is a tremendously fun film with lots of heart and endearing characters. I very much look forward to seeing it again.

title: Just About OK!
review:
Whilst I was watching this movie I was vaguely entertained but now having left the auditorium some things were far from satisfactory.

I will detail my concerns in order;

1.Brie Larson, quoting Dorothy Parker "she runs the gamut of emotions from A to B", there was absolutely no range in her acting. When your main character in a superhero movie just doesn't cut it and the whole movie rests upon this character your in big trouble.

2.This is an origin story and yet most of the questions surrounding her origins remain unanswered. We have no clue as to why she is so powerful, what are her specific powers apart from energy manipulation of all sorts, she is a kind of superhero "one-trick-pony"(that was clever).

3.Captain Marvel is apparently so powerful and has no weaknesses, unlike Superman and Kryptonite, or overcome by superior strengths as with Dr Strange, Spiderman, and the Hulk. To have no weaknesses whatsoever ruins the movie, as there is no point where you feel she is in any danger of losing against her enemies or indeed any danger at all. The only apparent weakness she seems to have was a whole array of cognitive problems, poor memory, brainwashing, poor judgement and trust issues (I have those before my first coffee).

4.Brie Larson just does not look the part, a Bond girl must look like a Bond girl and a superhero woman must look like a superhero woman (unless she is, of course an anti-hero). Without be overly judgemental or hung up on stereotypical images at best she looked ordinary when she needed to look extraordinary (Shock horror I made that point!). She will not be going up on any pre-pubescent teenage bedroom walls methinks (and again!)

5.I won't dwell on other problematic areas like, a clumsy plot, slow pace, embarrassingly cheesy jokes, no character development or poor music or indeed the strange over-long, un-productive, uninteresting and boring conversations they have with each other (I've dozed off!).

6.The movie is so over-contrived to make her a worthy opponent for Thanos that we just felt the whole movie was in a waiting room, a precursor to the main event.

The one thing that was totally memorable and sticks in my mind, and is worthy of a major mention and displayed both a remarkable acting ability and a whole variety of different powers and abilities was the ginger cat. Could we not put the cat against Thanos in the next movie, I am sure he would win, I can clearly see the scene where Thanos, the planet killer, is defeated by a regurgitated fur-ball to the head (what an image).

title: A solid watch and a lot of fun
review:
So happy I chose to spend International Woman's Day with the most badass woman in the galaxy!

For anyone who's interested, here's my spoiler free review...

Lemme start by saying, I haven't read comics in a very long time, and Captain Marvel was never on my radar, so any liberties taken from the comics didn't bother me whatsoever. Took me a little while to get into it, but when I did, I was ALL IN. The de-aging technology is seamless. The effects were solid. Skrulls looked dope. Personally, it was my favorite Stan Lee cameo of the MCU. The 90s soundtrack kicked ass! Brie Larson was a little bit snarky, but I dug it. Take your daughter. Take your niece. It's important for them to see badass women doing badass thing. Two thumbs up. I rate it a solid 8/10.

PS. One mid credits scene, stay for it. One post credits scene, funny, but if you need to pee, skip it.

title: Oh so bland...
review:
Very mediocre movie. Lousy acting from the lead actor. Very few intended jokes are actually funny. It's a good storyline, but poorly told. No part of it is impressive. Even the music and score is absolutely unappreciable. Not in keeping with the Marvel style at all.
Basically, not at all worth watching and spending money on. Extremely disappointing.

title: Good Marvel's Origin
review: I liked this film.I was not bored while watching it. I liked Brie Larson's acting.So I don't see any causes to hate this movie. In my humble opinion, it's typical Marvel's origin. title: Show was stolen by the cat and Jackson.
review:
Brie's Carol Danvers shows little emotional range that doesn't feel forced. Her jokes and humor elicited almost nothing on opening night in Alamo Drafthouse - people had 1-2 drinks and should have been a little looser than normal, yeah?

The 90's nostalgia seems like it's would go over this younger generations head, although it helped me enjoy it just a little more. A

title: Women power
review:
Fantastic character buildup typical of Marvel....
Captain Marvel is a better version of Wonder woman in a parallel universe..

title: Unbiased review - Unrealised potential.
review:
I personally like to think I tuned out the politics around the movie and I personally didn't know of Brie Larsen so I went into the movie with a fresh perspective. This movie didn't have a good structure, in my opinion it started quite well but as the movie went on it was quite a drag. Very little was done to develop the movie, for example, the war between the Kree and the Skrull, I was very disappointed with how this wasn't explored and virtually no reasons were given as to the basis for the war, the motivations of the Kree to rid the skrulls or what the skrulls may have done to piss off the Kree. I kid you not, it only takes 2 minutes to explain this, considering the plot twist later on in the movie with the Skrulls, the ideal opportunity to explain the context behind the war was at the beginning of the movie with the Kree, their motivations could have been explained further as to what the Skrulls May have done to them. They could have done this and it would not haven taken away from the plot twist.

Then there was Brie Larsen, I personally felt her character wasn't written well and this role was in my opinion, beneath her in all honesty. She wasn't given much to work with, I felt that she also didn't see the potential in Captain Marvel as there were scenes in the movie where she could performed better. Take for example the lunchbox scene which was presumed by Gron Rog (sorry if I spelt that wrong) to have contained the Tessaract, when it was revealed that there is no Tessaract, I personally thought this was a real comedic moment where she could have eased up her posture and pretended to be surprised by saying "what, But what, I could have sworn that damn Skrull put it in there" it was very underwhelming for me. But I must stress, this was not Brie's undoing, I would be unmotivated too if I read a script where I get powers and there is no explanation as to why I got them. Okay she was blasted with the core energy and she absorbed it but why was she able to and not others, what separated her from everyone else. I rather watch Plank from Ed Edd and Eddy, now that was a well developed character. This poor character development really hindered Brie Larsen's ability to actually act and infuse a personality to the character. I personally saw her potential with the emotion she showed when she was united with Maria, she done really well portraying her sadness and really sent the message of, I'm sad because I can't remember, this was the only potential to give the character a bit of range and she done well, but she isn't super actor - the saviour of all characters, there is so much she could do. I would love to nitpick other scenes but it wasn't entirely Brie's fault.

Overall, the movie really thanked, I am not even gonna get into the Tessaract questions and how Marvell came into possession of it (this too was unexplored) as we know Howard Stark was in possession of it and this was why it sucked because they didn't spend time to develop it. If I was to compare this to the first Thor movie which in my opinion sucked, but it only sucked for me because there was not enough action but every character had range and there was a great piece of story telling behind it. This is nothing like the first Thor movie, in fact I felt like I committed a crime to even compare the two. 3/10 for me so I wouldn't recommend anyone to go see it.

title: This is a great movie
review: I went into this movie after reading reviews saying it wasnt very good....i was shocked to discover it was a great mivje with the usual brill special effects and action you come to expect from marvel movies....i would definitely reccomend this as a taster for avengers end game in a few weeks

title: Bland at best.
review: Brie Larson is mediocre at best. She does not portray a "warrior/soldier" mentality. Her fights scenes seem over CGI to make up for her limited skill in the physical department. Even Samuel L Jackson puts in a rather boring performance. He portrays a bumbling fool for most the movie. The villains are rather poor interpretations of their comic counterparts. The prosthetics make their speech inaudible at times. They also didnt really have a real direction or purpose for their actions besides very loose ideals. The presentation and back story for the main character is the only bright spot but its watered down by the poor acting of Larson.

title: Captain Meh!
review: The movie is just okay. Better the TLJ, but still not up to the level of other MCU films. It could've been a lot better. But like TLJ, what's frustrating is changing the lore to fit a narrative that didn't need to be there. The marketing and comments of the people involved in a film matter to a viewer's opinion. For that reason I marked the movie lower. Stay true to the roots of your stories.

title: Fab film
review: Absolutely loved this film, don't understand all the negative reviews it's getting

title: Family Fun/Connective Tissue for the MCU
review:
My family and I felt it was actioned packed and funny! Captain Marvel provided the appropriate link between Agents of SHIELD/Guardians of the Galaxy/Infinity War. Also, a good tie-in for End Game.

Brie Larson's performance I felt was played appropriately strong, humorous, and balanced. In my opinion she had this ever-present collectiveness about her character (very Jedi-like), even though her emotions are part of her strength and power. This is as very military persona she portrayed, which was in line with both halves of her character (USAF/Kree).

Samuel L. Jackson's performance was superb. I believe all audiences had been waiting to see Fury's early years and steps towards leaders of SHIELD.

Lashana Lynch's performance was outstanding and provided the grounded-reality to the movie. Her emotional scenes with both Larson and Akira Akbar are powerful...bringing the emotional spark and connection to the film. She also delivered strong leadership in crisis situations.

Ben Mendelsohn continues to deliver strong villain performances; however, I was pleasantly surprised with the turn of his character through the film. Mendelsohn's emotional range provided the perfect package for Talos.

review: Brie's performance was similar to that of the actor in the Netflix Iron Fist series. She could not convince herself as a hero. Weak script and awful explanation of his absence from Earth for so long.

review:

They showed a good story, nice plot, nice pictures, nice sounds as always.

But this is what they lack. I nice personality of the movie. title: Wow was I surprised!
review:
I admit I was excited to go see Captain Marvel when the first trailer hit as it was obviously important to the next Avengers movie, but the bad press really turned me off and was going to wait to see it at some point. The family and neighbors wanted to see it tonight so we did.

I was really surprised at what a good movie it was as it was way more entertaining and funny than I thought it would be. I don't think Brie Larson was the best pick for this movie but the others were pretty darn good.

title: Cool effects but pretty forgettable.
review: Mendelsohn was a solid choice, he had some great moments. I did appreciate the 90s nostalgia theme and humor. Overall though the story and acting weren't terribly memorable. The special effects are on par with other Marvel movies. I wouldn't discourage anyone from seeing Captain Marvel but its just not going to be on my list of favorites.

title: If you want to watch a strong female movie, watch wonder woman or alita
review: I wish I slept in, I wish I had seen the future so I could get my time back. Forget the sexism, racism, the politics, this wasnt a marvel movie, this was a movie with a avg script and avg lead role. Thank god for samuel jackson

title: This movie doesn't deserve the hate
review:
Yes, Brie Larson ruined months of marketing with a single sentence, but that doesn't mean the movie needs to be that disregarded because she made a stupid mistake.
The movie is well done. Not the best marvel movie, but one of the best origin story ones.
The actress that plays Captain Marvel doesn't perform that well, but the other cast is exceptional. The visual effects looks good and the story has an interesting twist (differed from the one in the comics ).
The marvel quality is still there, so when watching the movie think about all the other talented people that worked on it and forget about the whole drama and propaganda that is happening in the "real world".

title: Don't understand the hate
review: Watch the movie, politics and drama aside, I bet you'll be entertained. Admittedly not a stand out film, but we shouldn't expect Infinity War quality for a set up movie. Nothing was irritatingly bad (besides a few CGI scenes), a solid 7.

title: A Fitting Tribute to Stan Lee - Captain Marvel
review: I honestly hadn't seen any reviews on Captain Marvel before seeing the movie. So upon reading it was receiving average scores was surprising. I really enjoyed this origin story for a character I knew nothing about. I've never read the comics so can't say if it paid justice to the comic character. But i didn't care. The movie was entertaining, funny and followed Marvel's winning formula. The plot tied up a few loose ends in the Marvel movie franchise storyline such as how the Tesseract was on Earth, and how Nic Fury lost his eye. All in all if you've enjoyed watching all the Marvel movies so far you won't be disappointed with this one.

title: Ok intro story good, Larson inconsistent but fine
review:
The story is interesting and equivalent to many other origin stories. Not as good as iron man or black panther but on par with thor probably. Maybe you need more spectacle though post avengers infinity war.

Larson rushes her comedy lines and some of the heart felt arc with her friend slowed the story down. I wanted the more aggressive Captain marvel from the comics where she can lose her temper. However when she gets going she can be pretty hardcore esp near the end.

Directors are a bit pedestrian jude law and Jackson did a good job.

title: An average film overshadowed by the star's political agenda
review:
I saw this on it's opening movie last night. I tried my hardest to ignore all of the behind-the-scenes ideology and just enjoy the movie in it's own right.

Unfortunately, I simply could not do this. The film was incredibly slow with lengthy exposition scenes and flashbacks used to create the origin story, and the buddy cop style movie that filled the rest of the time was fine, but lacked when compared to the 80's and 90's movies like Lethal Weapon, Point Break etc.

Stan Lee's cameo was good, but raises a lot of questions (so Stan Lee plays Stan Lee in a world of characters that Stan Lee created..?). Samuel L Jackson was okay, but no better than in his other recent films, such as The Hitman's Bodyguard (a NetFlix movie). But Brie Larson could have been replaced by a cardboard cut-out and nobody would have been able to tell the difference. The most enjoyable character for me was the cat. And when a cat is the star of the movie, that isn't a good sign!

The icing on the cake that made me groan were the pro-feminist messages scattered throughout the movie, such as No Doubt's 'Just A Girl' playing over the final battle, and many of the male characters being portrayed as misogynists (one character referencing the plane's 'cockpit', for example). It was moments like these that bought Larson's political agenda crashing back into the picture and made me cringe. I honestly feel that if Marvel had chosen another actress (or at least told Larson to hold back on her controversial statements regarding men prior to the film's release) that people would have been a lot more willing to overlook these scenes.

All in all, this turned out to be an average film overshadowed by the star's political agenda. It is worth a watch - just to plug the gap between Infinity War and Endgame - but do not expect the next Thor: Ragnarok or Spider-man: Homecoming.

title: A Flight In The Right Direction
review: My honest opinion it was a good movie I enjoyed it from start to finish. The comedy was ok. the soundtrack was good. I enjoyed the fight scenes and really liked all the throwbacks. And it ties in with the Avengers End Game. I went it with a clear mind even with all the bad press and it's worth a watch.

title: Hail The Captain
review: Loved it! Thanos is done!!!! Nice overall feel though it wasnt the best marvel movie.

title: Poor main character writing ruins a potentially great movie.
review:
The script and the acting in general were not bad, lots of funny moments and interesting connections to the rest of the Marvel movies. Unfortunately, the main character is the movie's main problem.
The acting from Brie was boring and shallow at best and the character itself came off as very irritating. Very little character growth happens throughout the film and the origins of her powers seem questionable. She has virtually no weaknesses or failings and honestly this ruined the movie for me. When the hero can just magically do anything without any effort it is just cheap and lazy writing.
7/10 movie, but Brie's character knocks it down to a 3/10. I expect much better for Endgame.

title: Nothing new
review:
The movie is nothing new to the Marvel cinematic universe. In my opinion, some characters are loosely similar to other mcu ones (e.g. Korath and Drax).
I am not a fan of Brie at all. However, I have to say that Brie Larson's acting was better than what trailers showed us. She delivers good humor and action. Still, I think she could do better as Captain Marvel and I hope she'll do better in future mcu movies.
Captain Marvel fills some holes and answers questions we've been asking for a long period of time - e. g. what happened to Fury's eye - and that's one of the good things about this movie.
SGI is also very well done. I don't think this is the worst movie of mcu but it is not the best one either and I do believe that Brie has some work to do with her acting.

title: This Movie is One of The Greatest MCU Movie!
review:
Tbh, I'm not too excited about this movie in the first place. My only reason is for understanding things before Avengers EndGame(in case anything important comes from this movie). I watch at the cinema in the first day, cause I dont want to get a spoiler. After I watch the movie, OMG THIS IS SO DAMN COOL. I can't describe in words. It's the only MCU movie that blow my mind with that plot twist, Good job Anna&Ryan. The three main aspect of a great movie is :
