title: I wish it were better!
review:
I'm not sure how to express my opinions about this movie. It's definitely not bad, but it's lacking to say the least. I think the main issue was that the directors/writers relied on the classic MCU elements too much while trying to create an "out of the box" character. Ironically, the character arc was extremely cliche. Normally, I wouldn't have a problem with that but, the execution of the arc had many flaws too. People in my theatre were literally groaning during a particular scene in the final act.

However, the movie had good moments. Brie Larson wasn't at her peak performance, but her chemistry with Samuel L. Jackson was on point. Their interactions were the saving graces of the movie. The comedy wasn't cringy (most of the time), plus the de-aging CGI was seamless and Goose the cat was great. I'm also grateful that the movie wasn't too preachy and allowed Captain Marvel's actions to speak for themselves.

Overall, I wish that the character arc was more original/ better executed. Captain Marvel is a late comer in the MCU. Thus, character development needed more screen time for the audience to get to know Carol Denvers. At this point the character is just a deus ex machina which is a huge step backwards for the MCU.

title: Is everyone being a sheep or not?
review:
I know it's been a long time and I must be honest with you... Laziness got better of me, but no more pointless talking about me and let's dive right into this movie.

I don't expect you to know a lot about Captain Marvel, but if you haven't lived under the rock during the last few months, then you must surely know that Brie Larson wears the blue and red colours of the main heroine. And there's been a lot of controversy surrounding this Oscar winning actress and to be completely honest I'm glad that I didn't know too much about the drama before watching the movie. Many people on the internet have blamed this movie for the poor choice of the actress, the overwhelming dose of feminism and just throwing the movie under the bus in general. I mean, I know people that chose to see Alita instead of Captain Marvel, just because of Brie Larson being in the movie. However, after watching the movie I spent almost one hour looking at all the hot topics floating around, and it made me notice some flaws that I didn't spot during or right after finishing the movie.

Well, people should have their own opinion, right? I feel like that people got swayed by the opinion of general public way too much and didn't give this movie a chance it deserves. Let me tell you something, this blockbuster isn't as bad as people say and I'm happy that I wasn't a sheep like many others.

For the first time in a long time I wasn't feeling the score. I'm sorry Marvel, it wasn't just doing it to me. In my opinion, the music should either give me chills, tear me up or make me stomp my feet. Well, nothing happened. What a shame.

90's was the time setting of the movie, well that's what they told you. You could see old stunning cars and old school clothes, but I wanted more. Give me some classy music that makes my hips uncontrollable and old pleasing commercials for Coca Cola. The should have watched Bumblebee, that's a recipe how to portray 80's and 90's.

Time to give credit where credit is due. Hands down, people behind the VFX, brilliant job once again. Hala looked stunning with its majestic building and spaceships flying around. It felt like experiencing Asgard once again. Ahhh, poor Asgard... And the space battle at the end? Oh boy, I travelled back in time to witness Han Solo destroying Stormtroopers from the sky. The feels.

I hope you're still awake, because this review is far from being over. Here's a list of the characters, from the best to the worst.

Maria Rambeau (Lashana Lynch)

The side character being on the top of my list? That's weird right? Well not really. Maria was a type of person, that Carol Danvers should have been. What I'm trying to say here? You could believe that the character could be real. From her being badass, which wasn't forced to the audience, but excellently displayed by her ability to control the fighter jet and doing the right decisions at the right time, to her showing emotions that made you sympathise with her. Overall, outstanding performance by Mrs. Lynch.

Stan Lee

I wouldn't normally include Stan in the list, but after what Marvel did at beginning, I have to. It was super sweet and teary at the same time. Seeing the compilation of all Stan's appearances in the MCU, with the Marvel logo we know and love slowly building up on the screen and the goosbumpy music in the background. You got me there Marvel. If this scene didn't make me tear up, the second one surely did. I was enthusiastically waiting for his nowadays traditional ten seconds scene in every movie and let me tell you, this one hits really close to hearth. The interaction between Stan a Marvel was something truly magnificent, even though it was only a nod towards Stan. You could feel the emotions, even though neither of them said a word. Bravo!

Talos/Keller (Ben Mendelsohn)

Everyone expected Samuel L. Jackson to be the humorous factor of the movie. He was, but Ben M. did a better job, both as Talos and Keller, Fury's boss in S.H.I.E.L.D. After the twist that Skrulls are the good guys (I kind of anticipated that from watching Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.), Talos teamed up with Carol and the squad. His jokes were on point and the interactions especially with Fury were top notch.

Monica Rambeau (Akira Akbar/Azari Akbar)

It's always hard to judge kid's performance so I feel obligated to mention a good one if I see one. Akira's portrayal of Marias daughter was truly quality performance and if Kevin Feige will eventually decide to introduce Spectrum (older Monica Rambeau), the actress chosen to play her will have big shoes to fill.

Carol Denvers/Vers/Captain Marvel (Brie Larson)

You must have been wondering, where the hell is Captain Marvel. She must be on the top, because she's the main character, right? Well, that's unfortunately not the case. From the start, you have to get use to her behaviour, which comes something as a surprise, but not a pleasant one. Her way of interacting with other characters feels somewhat cocky and egoistic, something I wasn't expecting from her character going into the movie. I couldn't figure out where I saw that kind of behaviour before and then it suddenly hit me. She's trying to act like Iron Man. "Hey, what's the problem", you might say. Iron Man is awesome! What's wrong with her being cocky. I'll tell you where's the problem. When it came to emotional scenes with Robert Downey Junior, you could believe that he was suffering and going through hard times. That wasn't happening with Carol, especially in the scene where she finally discovered what happened to her on Earth. It was just weak, not believable at all. I think it's not 100percent Larson's fault, the way the character itself is written played a huge part in it.

Earlier I spoke about the flaws I noticed after going on the internet. These missteps were slight signs of feminism. Wait, don't throw rocks at me yet, before I say anything else, I don't think that there were that many feminist moments as people say, but there were some, that didn't have to be there that ruined the overall experience. I'm talking about the ending scene with Fury, where he decided to name the Avengers initiative after Carol. I mean, did Marvel forget about Captain America: The first Avenger? Should it be The second Avenger now? The second scene is where she stood up against the Supreme Intelligence, remembering her past, where she always had to stand up after being laugh at, wait for it, by white men. I mean, did you really have to do us like that? C'mon Marvel...

The last things that felt a little bit of was the scene where she finally harnessed her full powers. Don't get me wrong, I had massive goose bumps watching that scene. But shouldn't she be a little bit clunky, using her newly discovered powers for the first time? She was flying in the skies like a pro, having zero problems, even though that was her first time flying. She for sure feels overpowered, which is kind of worrying and it makes you think how the MCU will deal with her powers compared to the other Avengers in End Game, because she is definitely the strongest one right now.

Nick Fury (Samuel L. Jackson)

Like I said before, it was expected from Nick Fury to be the funny character and he was. But his humour was slowly decreasing throughout the course of the movie, with Talos doing a better job and replacing him. Fury's jokes slowly became cringy and forced, but I would still rank him at the same level as Carol.

Phill Coulson (Clark Gregg)

The producers teased us with Phill being in this movie and I was all for it. If you know me, and if you don't, let me tell you something, I'm sucker for Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. and my boy Coulson, but the producers literally bamboozled us. All we got were three scenes? My boy deserved better than this.

The Supreme Intelligence/Mar-Vell/Dr.Wendy Lawson (Annette Bening)

Even though the concept of the Supreme Intelligence was cool, it didn't live up to its full potential. They honestly could have done more, it's the head of the Kree, isn't it? When it comes to Mar-Vell, I don't mind that the producers changed the gender of the character from man to woman, I'm completely fine with that, but despite the fact she played a huge part in the story, she hardly ever appeared on the screen.

Yonn-Rogg + the Kree group

I expected the Kree to be the bad guys, but it still didn't change the fact that they were so damn boring.Yonn-Rogg looked promising at the beginning, but the fact that he acted the same way throughout the whole movie made him so unenjoyable to watch. And there is no point talking about the rest of the Kree, they were just extras, I'm sorry. The main villains, more like the main...nothing.

Goose/Flerken

The crowd favourite and pleaser. Why everyone loves this cat so much? I wasn't a fan and I'm still not. title: Don't listen to the haters
review:
Quick review: The tepid reviews of this film are so revealing. Reality: it's as good as any MCU movie and in fact it's better than most of them. Apparently some people just can't deal with female leads.

Longer version: Wow. The reviews for Captain Marvel are so depressing - even the good ones.

I love Marvel MCU films. I also know they are "just entertainment" for most audiences and, even at their best, they are not especially deep or meaningful. I think of them as a sort of glittering disco ball approach to movie making. If you love comics and science fiction, as I do, then you get some extra geek enjoyment. They have mastered a magic money making formula which seems completely fresh after over 20 films.

Captain Marvel is easily one of the best MCU films, reflecting a decade spent honing the formula and CGI. Yet even the good reviews are decidedly tepid. Worse, some describe the film as "sweet", which seems like about the worst chosen word I can imagine for Marvel's first female led film. Whatever next, "helpful"?

Of course, the MCU is heavily male-dominated. This reflects the comics, the audience, and the creators. While it's clear Marvel have made some efforts to rebalance things, not least this film, there's no doubt that he MCU is running on testosterone. It's also a sort of pre-adolescent world in which relationships and sexuality are mostly absent. It's got its problems, for sure.

But apparently the folks at Marvel are nowhere near as caught up in the grip of patriarchy as some of their audience and, more depressingly, the overwhelming majority of film critics.

Captain Marvel is a pacy, energetic action film that delivers. It's in a similar genre, but more successful than, a host of other MCU films that have won much more enthusiastic reviews.

Yet here it is earning mostly yawns and faint praise. "It's fine" says Mark Kermode defensively. The fan reviews say it is "boring".

I cannot imagine any possible explanation for this other than deep rooted sexism and misogny: It's seen as boring because it is about female characters. Massive face palm.

title: My 3 arguments against these negative Nancys
review:
After reading the negative comments, I still decided to go spend money on this movie. I didn't like the trailer but I trust MCU. I'm glad I did because I loved the movie! I have 3 arguments to share against all of these negative reviews-

1.) Everyone complains about how Carol Danvers is too powerful but she wasn't at first? Her struggle was not believing in herself and not being sure on who she was. And then there's people trying to push her down and keep her down. And the people were mainly men but it makes sense why. Comments like "you run like a girl" or "girls aren't as strong as boys" were common when I grew up and caused me to be insecure about things. Danvers weakness is something that girls are used to. This isn't just a "Girl Power" movie though. Danvers herself says "I'm proud to be human" before she gets her full strength. Everyone has been pushed down in their life and felt less of a person because of it. But you always try to get back up and be resilient and Danvers literally does stand up to the plate.

Danvers resilence and finding her identity is extremely powerful. I had goosebumps and a sense of pride when she finally got her full strength. The display of her "over powerfulness" is to show that she is going to be a worthy component against Thanos.

2.) Also, some of the reviews claim Danvers didn't have a good back story? How can they write a back story if she can't remember her backstory? And did we really want to see a backstory during the middle of the movie? It was better for it to be a mystery. And her character deveopment was perfect. Going back to my first argument: A.) she learned who she was B.)she learned she wasn't going to hold back for anyone C.) she learned who to always be resilient like she was before her memory swipe. -THAT IS DEVELOPMENT-



3.) My last argument is the comparison of Wonder Woman and Captain Marvel. Why do we constantly want to pit DC and Marvel against each other? Like why can't we enjoy both? And why do we have to compare two super women? Wouldn't it make more sense to compare Captain Marvel to another pilot in the D.C. universe (*cough* *cough* GREEN LANTERN). Just because two characters have two vaginas, doesn't mean they're automatically pitted against each other.



Go watch the movie yourself and formulate your own opinion. I loved it and found it kind of inspiring!

title: A short review of "Captain Marvel" (2019)
review:
"Captain Marvel" (2019) has a couple of weaknesses, but mostly rises above them in its second half to become an entertaining big-budget popcorn movie. It generally succeeds, and I had a lot of fun with it. I'd rate it an 8 out of 10.

At first, the movie comes off as a mild disappointment - a boilerplate, made-to-order space opera with a thin script, simplistic dialogue and sometimes average acting. (I personally don't think that Brie Larson has the most depth or range of any actress in Hollywood.)

But the movie has a few surprises for us, both in terms of its story and its ability to win us over with humor and its sense of escapist, comic book fun. Larson does have a lot of onscreen presence and charisma, and she does fine conveying anger and urgency. She also has great deadpan comic line delivery. After seeing the film, it's difficult for me to picture anyone else in the role.

The special effects were nothing short of fabulous. I didn't expect to see a Marvel film with a space battle that could compete with those of the "Star Wars" franchise. The fan service and the continuity with other Marvel films is also terrific. Speaking of fan service - the Stan Lee tributes were genuinely touching. One of them was a threefold reference to Lee, Kevin Smith and the 1990's, when the story is set. Talk about understanding how to please your target audience.

I'd recommend this.

title: My 7YO daughter and her 43YO dad (me) both loved it!
review:
I was almost caught up in the hype about the social justice agenda taking over this film, the character being too perfect and too powerful, Marvel getting a little too PC, but after the emotional gut-punch that was Infinity War it was the fun action flick that I never knew I wanted!

Positives: A good story, unfolding in cohesive acts that might feel a little long by the end but hits on all the marks. It adds a little backstory on some established MCU characters, provides an awesome 90's soundtrack, and delivers some solid action that (unlike a lot of superhero films) wasn't just a jumble of generic baddies being tossed around. The actions sequences weren't unnecessarily drawn out like they seem to be in some other films. And YES - it had multiple strong female characters besides the lead and THIS IS NOT A BAD THING. I'm raising a daughter here and I'm happy to see some girls and women lead the action. There are almost no movies with female heroes like this despite the Marvel Universe being full of them. I'm an old school Marvel Comics fan and admittedly a bit of a sexist myself and I have absolutely no problem with some serious kick ass female test pilots, soldiers, and cosmic ray emitting demigods taking the limelight. By the way, this film was fine for my 7 year old. There is an F-bomb and a bit of death and violence but it's a touch more kid friendly than most MCU films I'd say.

Negatives: it might be a tiny bit long but like I said the pacing seemed ok while watching the film with just a couple moments that seemed a bit slow. I was concerned about how compelling an overpowered character might be but the hero and her abilities worked.

Ignore the naysayers. We can all agree that Disney sh-t the bed on the new SW trilogy, but those complaints of Marvel being hijacked by a social justice agenda are total nonsense. This was a solid superhero film and a refreshing addition to the marvel cosmic mythology. Furthermore, if you dig the whole serial film concept like I do it's the perfect beat to stick between the two darker (presumably) Avengers Infinity War films. It fills in a little bit of necessary plot and gives us some good humour and action which is what Marvel has always been about. The ultimate message about heroism not being about powers but more about grit and the heart to keep getting up was just awesome. Take your kids to see this movie, get the large popcorn, and sit back & enjoy it.

title: Satisfying yet unbalanced
review:
This review was written on 03/08/2019.

No doubt, any MCU connection after several months of silence is anticipated for any fan who has followed the inception of the universe since 2008. This movie at this time is nonetheless subject to controversy given the potential interpretations of its politically-driven agenda.

"Captain Marvel" to be honest, was enjoyable and satisfying. Though I did not have high expectations for a movie introducing a new character shortly before the greatest upcoming movie of the MCU, this movie was very well a good addition and worth the time.

*****Beware, SPOILERS AHEAD*****

The Stan Lee tribute in the introduction is an indescribable satisfaction. Thoughtful, considerate and a strong way to begin.

CHARACTERS/ACTING: Brie Larson was a good choice. Her depiction of Captain Marvel/Carol Danvers was well played, with a strong physique and lovely smile. Nonetheless, whether it is an acting problem or a scripting issue, she didn't really balance being serious, under threat, silly, and humorous. The interchange between these expressions was too quick and lacked subtlety that it weakened her role and ridiculized the seriousness of some sequences. Many moments shared resemblance to Tony Stark's (Robert Downey Jr) debut, namely the first flight of the Mach II (the "whoooooo") and her first flight. He, nevertheless, was not dodging an alien invasion at the time and his expressions were concordant.

Nick Fury (Samuel L. Jackson) appeared too happy, lacked being serious and mostly appeared silly - a side we are not acquainted to. In the entirety of the movie, he did not have a leading role (understandable), but was unfortunately depicted as a damsel in distress.

The Skrull soldiers as a whole appeared too comical. Their spirit in most their fights was unserious and unfortunately ridiculous, posing the question if these are muppets or the terrifying Skrulls we anticipated.

STORY: The enigma who is "Vers" and its slow reveal was very well scripted, yet might have been fast forwarded at the end. Throughout the movie, unlocking her memories and her transformation from a fighter pilot to a Kree soldier was satisfying and unprecedented. Being taken hostage at her first mission is a bit disappointing though.

The evolution of the plot and the later twist was great, completely unanticipated, but might have been short on emotions reflective of purpose.

As for the long-anticipated story of how Nick Fury lost his eye, this was extremely disappointing: no pain? no agony? no strong comeback line? Such a useless, big, unsung loss. We're talking of the same eye referred to in the Winter Soldier movie.

IN-MOVIE MESSAGES: There is no denying the movie was strong on femininity. No doubt historically, women have not received their due rights easily and without fight, and this movie has a take-home message that Captain Marvel's powers lie in the oppressions she suffered from her male comrades. Nonetheless, women's rights were never an all-female initiative. This movie might have attempted to make Nick Fury as this supporting man, but the duo between him and Danvers seemed unbalanced, rendering him mostly dependent on her (of course he's not as powerful, but you don't need powers to be a hero right?). As a fan of this genre, gender never mattered nor it will. It is the heroes' developments, challenges, lessons and aspirations that leads to their grandeur and significance - NOT their gender. As such, the stress on solo female power was a bit excessive - none of the previous MCU characters ever hinted on a male exclusive domination. Nevertheless, though it started out strong on this, the movie's progression tuned it down and focused on what we are more accustomed to: heroism.

SUMMARY: The movie adds up to the collection of a decade of a universe in the making. Judging it, one might forget that this is an origin story film. One might have also forgotten that the last origin story was several several several years ago (2011: Captain America the first avenger; Black Panther was introduced in Civil War with the main guys). Judging it using the same criteria as the Avengers for example is therefore, unfair.

It is understandable that its timing in a period where half the universe is wiped off and where the Avengers are shattered, makes us more judgmental on its content as we ask ourselves where was she during the attack on New York and were all the challenges the avengers previously faced not "emergent" or worth a page?

Nonetheless, her role in Endgame is yet to be determined, as after all, she is merely the product of one infinity stone. Thanos possesses six.

title: "Captain Marvel" movie review: Watch it or skip it?
review:
What's up muthaclucks! So, I just finished watching Captain Marvel and I have to say it wasn't too bad. Before the movie starts, a new Marvel intro is played which features a collage of virtually every cameo Stan Lee starred in, which was a nice homage to the man who started it all. At the end of the intro, the whole theater was clapping and making noise which added to the excitement and anticipation.

The movie starts off with some good action scenes, but right off the bat I didn't know if I was going to like it based on how some of the alien characters looked. They just looked very strange and fake. What I mean by that is that when I see alien characters like Thanos, Groot, or Hulk, I forget that I'm watching a movie and I actually believe that the characters I'm seeing are real. That was not the case here and to be honest, it was a little distracting. But the aliens did end up winning me over by the end of the movie due to their numerous scenes full of humorous dialogue.

The fight scenes were good, but there were no memorable moments that stood out. It was just generic superhero fighting that I didn't feel invested in. There was just not enough of a story for me to care about these fight scenes. What also didn't help these fight scenes were the corny one liners the main character would say amid the fighting. Also, the main character went from just barely being able to hang with her enemies to becoming an absolute destroyer. It was just not believable that suddenly, she could wreck everyone and destroy whole ships at will.

The scenes that made the whole movie worth it were any that included Samuel L. Jackson. The chemistry he had with the cast was incredible in that he brings humor that doesn't feel forced to every scene. I don't know if that's what they were going for, but this movie felt more like a comedy instead of a serious build up to Avengers: Endgame. As for the story, there just wasn't much there. The plot twist did nothing for me, and the reason our hero is fighting didn't really move me. At the end of the movie I felt like something was missing. The movie was two hours long, but it felt like it could've been a little bit longer for the sake of developing the characters into something we could emotionally invest in.

Some other enjoyable aspects of the movie were all of the 90's nostalgia scenes. From the soundtrack, to the wardrobe, and to the scenes with businesses which were all the rage back in the day but no longer exists. It was a great feeling that brought back many memories. Those scenes didn't feel forced and were tied in with humor and a good soundtrack seamlessly to the movie.

My conclusion, this was a fun movie to watch. The funny scenes were good, the fight scenes were average, and the storyline was not something you felt emotionally invested in. The dramatic scenes felt forced, like they were just trying too hard and speaking in a way that normal people don't speak. If you want to know the origin story of Captain Marvel who is going to play a huge role in Avengers: Endgame, watch it. If you want to laugh for a few hours and don't care much for a story or serious acting, watch it. but just don't expect it to be as good as the last Avengers movie, it doesn't even come close. If you don't care about Marvel movies I would go ahead and skip this. Am I glad I watched it? Yes. Would I buy this when it comes out? No. All in all, I give this movie a 7.5 out of 10.

Don't forget to stick around after the movie is over, there is a mid-credits scene that is relevant to Avengers: Endgame. After that there is one more scene after the final credits roll that doesn't really have anything important but does provide a good laugh.

FINAL SCORE: 7.5/10

title: A Review from a MOVIE Fan Who Does Not Trust Fan Reviews
review:
The early reviews on IMDB and other sites made me not want to see this much anticipated (by me at least) movie. But when you read many of them you have to wonder - who gives a movie one star? There are not many 10/10 star movies but there are NO one star movies either.

I went to see Captain Marvel this afternoon to avoid the large crowds and was very happy with this move. Yes, the back story takes some time to build but unless you are a child, what's the matter with developing a story? There are several times during the early parts of the movie we go long periods of little to no dialog while the action commands the screen. This is very unlike a traditional Marvel movie when characters like Tony Stark, Thor or the crossover Deadpool can't shut up.

Brie Larson is perfect for the role and the script stays true to the Marvel Comics character. Following the Russo brother's direction, Anna Boden was able to fill gaps and add new information for the next Avenger's movie "End Game".

In the end, make your own decision. One-star reviews were posted well before the movie was even released to critics. A 7 or 8 star review is where this movie belongs. Not great, but it's an origin story setting up "End Games". So sit back, relax, and enjoy a very good movie.

title: Overhype
review:
First and foremost, the over sensitive reviews about feminism are way overblown, as are the over excited reviews about feminism. There really isn't that much in the movie. It's jusy a super hero movie where the hero happens to be a chick.

That said, up until the last 20 minutes - half hour or so, it was fairly enjoyable. But once she has her transformation at the end, she becomes basically Dr. Manhattan. All powerful, no weakness, and just boring. When there is no threat to a hero, the fun of a movie ends.

It was pretty middle of the road for MCU. It wasn't Iron Man 3 or Age of Ultron bad, but it also wasn't Ragnorok or Black Panther good. It's on par with Ant Man and the Wasp, or Winter Soldier. Not terrible, not great.

One thing that was really missing compared to other MCU movies was the humor. Not much here at all. Which was a bummer. There were also recycled bits from other movies. It isn't hard at all to see that some of Groot's homework was copied, just changed a little so the teacher wouldn't notice.

It's worth seeing if your local theater has a $5 movie night. But that's about it. No real impact on Endgame, so it's one that could even be tabled until home release.

title: It was a good and enjoyable movie
review:
So I went into this movie without knowing all of the political drama that led up to this movie. I was busy and did not have time to follow the internet drama. I went in excited as a fan of the marvel cinematic universe and I thought it was a great origin movie. I mean it wasn't the best by far but it was good movie to me.

I went online to see what others had to say about the movie and I feel like some are just a bit too hard on the movie? I mean I honestly thought it was good and I was engaged throughout the movie. Curious to see what really happened to her. Seeing young Samuel Jackson in action. And I really wasn't disappointed at all. I didn't expect such backlash from the film as I didn't know anything about the political drama.

I thought Brie Larson did a good job with Captain Marvel acting wise. I mean she played someone with a military background and trained by Krees for a while. It's not surprising that she isn't exactly all go lucky and a bit stoic. The moments where her compassion does show is nice. When she has her moments with her best friend and her best friend's daughter, I thought it bittersweet that she couldn't remember them but understood that she had a life here. I think Brie did well and I look forward to seeing more of her in the future.

I also think that Samuel Jackson did an amazing job as young Nick Fury. I loved that he was with her most of the time there and that they worked together. Their chemistry was very good and I loved his interactions with Goose. I know that people say he's different but what do you expect from encountering aliens for the first time compared to year's later when finding aliens is jusy another Tuesday night to him. I understand why people were upset about how he got the eyepatch but I thought it was funny that he is embarrassed to tell people that a cat did it.

I can understand if there are somethings that aren't as strong like maybe it was too flashback heavy and the color scheme was a bit bland. But for the movie I thought it fine as it was partially somber.

Overall I thought it was a solid introduction to Captain Marvel and I'm very excited to see how the Russo Brothers handle her after she's had her powers for over 20 years in the movie universe.

title: Eye candy aplenty, but sometimes sloppy filmaking...
review: I was expecting a bit more from this. Visually the film delivers, its visuals sometimes bring to mind "what if Terrence Malick directed a film for Marvel"... However, the musical cues are not handled so deftly, ranging from the hamfisted to the plain cringe worthy (the use of "Come as you are" and "I'm just a girl" is at best intrusive), and some scenes seem to lack a purpose or resolution (the french connection style pursuit looks like it was cut to make up for time)... Regarding the acting, Ben Mendelsohn pulls a solid performance, Brie Larson does an adequate job of the superpowered hero trope who tries to find herself and her place in the world, sometimes acting like a fish out of water (Star Trek IV, Terminator 2...), although it feels a bit wooden. One of the problems is that although "emotionality" is patent throughout the film, there isn't really any growth or development. Although circumstances change, the characters remain basically the same. It makes for an entertaining film, but it's not Marvel's best. You do get to hear Samuel Jackson singing the Marvelletes which is awesome though!

title: Good, story, good acting, butch hero Captain Marvel
review:
My partner and I enjoyed ourselves with this movie. Long ago, I've read the origin stories of the "original" Captain Marvel and his successor Ms. Marvel, and this movie has little to do with either of them (maybe with some later reboot of her origin story, but I haven't read those stories yet). The story in the movie is a very nice self-contained original reboot, set up with nice internal logic, and as many of the movie industry's superheroes undergo a reboot semi-regularly, this one is especially beautifully crafted.

Of course Stan Lee is in there. Nicely done. The movie even starts with him: the "Marvel" comic book sequence at the start contains a lot of different Stan Lee's and a lot of his quotes over the years.

This movie also stars younger versions of Agent Coulson and director Fury and they look stunning.

Brie Larson plays a butch woman, beautiful, self-assured, well-trained, with lots of character development, and different roles portraying different parts of her life: Carol Denvers, Vers, Captain Marvel. I also liked that she did not want to depend on other people. That she did not fall in love with some awesome man. That she took care of herself and others. A real hero.

I like the story development. The Kree are good, the Skrull evil, and and before that and later it seems vice-versa. Carol was human, than Kree, than human again, and now I think she might be a hybrid. There's a lot of shooting and of course the heroes aim better than the bad people. The cat, Goose, is one to pay attention to. Also, don't leave the cinema until the scene after all the credits ended, because, again, cat.

Some days ago I read that this movie amassed 455 million dollars during its opening weekend in the USA (plus what the movie made worldwide). Cool. I guess that means there will be at least one sequel. I look forward to see this integrated into the Marvel Cinematic Universe, like in the movie Avengers: Endgame which will be released next month.

title: Captain OP
review:
So I just watched Captain Marvel yesterday and I decided to post this review. There were 5 things that I didn't like: 1) The plot was far too confusing (especially in the first half of the movie) but you start to figure things out in the last 30 minutes. 2) We never get a good enough explanation about all of her powers, just that she was given these powers from the blast that occurred after she shot the plane's engine the day Mar-Vell died. 3) I think that the only characters that are genuinely interesting in the film are Fury, Coulson and Talos. Carol Danvers has some good moments in the film but overall she seems to be bored throughout most of the film. Brie Larson, even though she is a good actress, might not have been the best fit for the role. 4) Captain Marvel is WAY too overpowered! I mean in no point after she controls her powers do we feel that she can even get hurt, let alone get killed. That's one thing that I don't like about Superman and even he has a weakness (cryptonite). We never see anything that can even put a scratch on Captain Marvel, so that makes the fight sequences seem a little underwhelming. 5) The last thing that I didn't like was the not-so-subtle feminist-SJW propaganda throughout the film. Ok, we got it the first time, can we stop seeing the same scenes over and over again please?...

Overall, the movie had some funny moments, some good characters and let us know about the origin of Captain Marvel. It was ok to watch the film once, but I don't think it has any real re-watch value...

It was however not as good as Iron Man 1, all Captain American movies, Thor 3, all Avengers movies, all Guardians of the galaxy movies, Spiderman homecoming, and Black Panther.

Is she strong? It seems so. In this movie it felt like she had no match.

Is she Stronger than Captain America? Again on a boxing fight, Captain America seems stronger, it's only if she uses lasers that she could beat him.

Stronger than IronMan? Well Iron Man seems smarter and that is his main strength. He could probably figure out how to beat Captain Marvel by using his intelligence. But overall yes Captain Marvel is stronger than him.

Stronger than Black Panther? I wonder if Vibranium can take lasers with no actual damage. I think Captain Marvel is faster and can fly which makes her challenging to fight, but physically speaking I think Black Panther is stronger

Stronger than Thanos? Probably not. Thanos is much stronger physically speaking and her lasers can be defeated by the power of the infinity gauntlet.

Stronger than Doctor Strange? I think Doctor Strange using his intelligence and his magic tricks can put an interesting fight vs captain marvel. Similar to the one with Thanos. I'd say they are equal.

I would have preferred to see the few minutes of story we needed to see as a B Plot in another movie, maybe Guardians 3. Let's hope the movie is necessary for future Skrull or Kree movies.

The Fury eye reveal made me roll my eyes in disappointment. The tesseract being the mcguffin made me groan. The independent women anvil was cringworthy. The plot was predictable and dull and.... Pointless. One of the first long scenes had me moving around in my seat, bored already.

In terms of action and fight sequences it's similar in scale to phase one movies but with a bigger budget for effects. 8 years ago it would have been a decent entry but here and now it's like they're treading water and wasting time while they finish Endgame.

With this, Antman and The Wasp and Black Panther in a short space of time, Marvel is no longer the studio that guarantees a good time. They may be victims of their own success; in a world where we expect bigger and better every time, they've nowhere to go but down. These smaller scale movies with no real jeopardy feel like stale cash grabs.

title: Good but not as good as any other form MCU
review: The action scenes and all CGI was great as it always is for Marvel and story was fairly decent. But comments about Brie Larson lacking emotion and authenticity are very much true - the main protagonists weren't able to make me like or dislike her nor develop any other emotions towards her. The quality of humor seemed not good as in other Marvel movies but was all right overall. It is hard to review this movie objectively due all the controversy but I guess it is fair to say that it's not as good as any others form MCU but still worth watching.

title: Not great - but not for reasons you heard...
review:
Captain Marvel is a good movie. It's just not a good Marvel movie... A lot of writers/producers/studios, sometimes forget that their audience is - well - humans. In order to introduce a new character in a universe that is o so successful, you not only need a great crew (which includes, casts, writers etc etc.) but you have to understand the state of the viewer. This movie can be broken down on these two categories. 30% Women statement - and all this modern agenda, and 70% superhero movie. The problem is not the 30%... It is the 70% and then the other 30%... Marvel changed their storytelling from serious Captain Blackbeard to Captain Doodlemonster. Which works great on pumped up characters and already established powerful ones... But when you take the same formula, and put it on a new superhero, one that the viewer has not a single idea about - things tend to go messy.
  • N.1 Characters
It is sad to see Marvel not using its cast into its maximum. What was Fury doing in that movie? Absolutely nothing. Someone that I actually have a lot of respect - someone that I know that he means business , acted like a sidekick. No - less than that. He was the cat's babysitter. That was useful. If he wasn't in this movie, I wouldn't be surprised. Replace Nick with Happy and there is no flaw. Only Happy doesn't carry the same respect as Fury. I expect him to be, goofy - a bit out of place. Nick is supposed to be this well informed - always ahead of other type of leader. Why throw this out of the box and rewrite him as a cool to hang out guy? Just sad...
  • N.2 Rhythm
The movie started out great, until we meet Maria. Then all the plot gets boring. A great example is the barn scene. Mrs. Marvel was introduced on the first half as a hard to knock character but fun to stuck with. Why is she crying all of the sudden? She just survived a mind interrogation, blew a hole out of a spaceship, landed safely FROM SPACE on Earth - kicked ass with her arm power abilities , WHY IS SHE SUDDENLY CRYING! Why she does not believe in her self when she just has to read some numbers from a CD. Why do I need to see a "You are a female - you are strooooong" when I already know that? She kicks ass - stop reminding me stuff... Then we are back in the house and guess what? Skrull explains AGAIN why he needs her help. WE GET IT - WHERE IS THE SKIP 5 SECONDS BUTTON!!!!! Another example is the fight scene. Instead of showing me a good executed battle sequence with great hand to hand combat and magic arm ability moves, you choose to kick all this stuff out and show me how great Mrs.Marvel is... Again... I just show her removing the "Chip" and gaining full access to the overdrive... I know she is crazy powerful... Give me some well constructed action. Give me blood, give me gore, give me Captain America VS Loki action. GIVE ME MARVEL. In fact, the movie was keep showing me the same thing over and over again, that the actual plot twist was completely ignored! Kree are bad and Skrulls are good? K what is next? Yes I know that this is not a cat.... NEEEEEXT!
  • N.3 Audience stupidity
Remember back in Iron Man 2 where we get introduced to black widow? She was full of control when she entered the room and the audience noticed that. Then her action scene in Justin Harper's HQ? Her character was established right there as strong, powerful and full of respect. Captain Marvel misses that last part... Respect. Here's why: NEW MARVEL FORMULA. Not the character but the studio. You don't have to think anymore when watching a movie. Everything is served right in front of you. Questions like "What is Nick Furry like. How much authority does he have" must be answered by the viewer while watching the movie. This new formula was implemented successfully in the past - but in movies with already known characters. In the movie Captain Marvel , everything is reminding you the same thing "Vers is strong" . Space battle? Vers is strong. Fight with the intelligence? Vers is strong. Vers VS Ronan? Vers is strong. And here comes the 30% I mentioned earlier. Nothing wrong with that - I want another strong female character in this universe... Black Widow was established as awesome in 1/4 of the time... Why do new movies think the viewers are idiots? Why do they show us the same stuff over and over and over again? Why do the hyper inflate the character's feelings just to make a point?
  • N.4 Reality.
When you watch a superhero movie, you expect to see stuff that can't be done. However, as a viewer, you let your mind and soul be touched by the movie. It's this interaction we have, that in the end lets us enjoy flying people, spaceships, neon laser explosions... That means that the movie must show us a story in a natural way. What do I mean by that? You accept that Superman can fly in his unique blue-red suit. It doesn't feel unnatural yet it manages to scratch your imagination. But make superman able to transform into a blue red shark with Neo-Atom powered engine - well that's what I am trying to say. Captain Marvel felt , unnatural. I did not expect Fury to be like that. I did not expect the little girl to watch Vers flying into the night sky at the end. It reminded my of Merlin saying "Goodbye l" to Nemo! It didn't feel human, it was... unexpected. ------ All in all, Captain Marvel had the opportunity to be an amazing new chapter of MCU, but fails completely. Good movie, but bad MCU movie.

PS. To those who just skipped the paragraphs - I am actually stating great facts that the movie review has nothing to do with any anti female agenda... The problems are (in shortness - :Many Repeats: :Not so clever script: :Bad movie writing: :Bad character progression: ... Thank you for reading :)

title: A very average and run of mill entry in the with some good things in it.
review: The movie is not terrible it has a few good scenes and things in that I really liked it, but it is overall a very forgettable and bland movie. Let's start with the positive aspects of the movie first. Samuel L Jackson is of course always fantastic in the movie even though the dialogue in the film isn't very funny and is sort of boring. Now to the negative aspects of the movie Captain Marvel her self is not very heroic at all in the movie and it tries so hard to make you care when you really don't,Most of this comes from the dialogue and Brie Larson herself her performance feels very wooden like she is just going through the motions of the character without much energy. review: This movie was adequate. Not really much to say. That being said, I cannot help but feel like this movie was made out of necessity instead of passion,at times feeling like it was made to help Endgame make sense but that is really about it. I don't read comics or know much about the Captain Marvel mythos, so perhaps I do not understand the finer plot points that a true MCU fan would pick up on and enjoy but it was just astoundingly adequate. Not mediocre, not great, just worth the $10 I spent to get in the theater.

review:

title: Captain Marvel is very upsetting
review:
Don't go into this film thinking you're gonna see a masterpiece. This film is your average Marvel movie, and by that I mean it's fine. It's not as shockingly amazing as Infinity War and it's not as stupidly bad as Thor: The Dark World. It's just fine. My rating has nothing to do with the film having a female lead; in fact, that might be the reason I'm giving the film an extra point. I think it's great that Hollywood is making these female lead superhero films, and I think they should continue to do so. But the movie itself falls short on pretty much every aspect of it. I'm not saying this film is trash and you shouldn't go see it. I can't tell you what to do or what not to do. I'm saying that in my own opinion, it's far from being a perfect film, and it's close to being a below-average experience.

I think the main issue for me was the pacing and the complete number of plot holes within the film that just ruins it for me. The third act was probably the weakest of the three because of how much was going on and how fast it passed by. A good example of this is the dang cat. All I thought in the theatre was, "WTF?". And it's not just because of the fact that Nick Fury has an eyepatch cuz of a stupid cat scratch, but also because we have no explanation on what the hell the cat is and where it came from. We just see him appear, we see him shoot tentacles out of his mouth, and no one questions it which is just flat out dumb and makes the whole entire cat as apart of the movie unnecessary. I honestly would've bought it if the cat happened to be a Skrull the whole time, which I was actually hoping for.

Another good example of the awful pacing is toward the end of the second act where Captain Marvel finds out the truth about her past and the Skrulls. Let me just say, the entire scene with her, her friend, and the Skrull is unbelievably forced. It was like a minute long and she already had everything under control after she found out she was lied to for years. This is not a realistic reaction, and if they put time and effort into this plot twist and how they resolved it, it would've been so much better.

Captain Marvel as a character is just bland and legit has no personality. And as mentioned, her reactions to things are really forced and feel fake, and it wasn't Brie Larson's fault. She's an amazing actress. The fault lies with mediocre writing. It legit makes me cringe just thinking about it. Her lines are always these cheesy one-liners meant to either motivate us or make us laugh, which this movie fails at doing. The point that Captain Marvel as a character is trying to advocate does not work, and I feel like the Russo Brothers will do a better job with her in Endgame.

And as for Nick Fury...I can just say that he seems like a completely different character in this film. I thought that he would change once he damaged his eye, but I was wrong. I don't really have to defend why Nick Fury's character fell short in this film. And again, it wasn't Sam L. Jackson's fault, it was the writing.

Overall, Captain Marvel is a Marvel movie by Marvel Studios starring Captain Marvel and her mentor Mar-Vel. It's not the worst film I've ever seen, but it's definitely not the best by a long shot. I hope my reasoning makes it clear as to why my rating is what it is.

Final Verdict: 5/10

title: A Marvel Movie Lacking the Marvel Charm
review:
The complaints about lackluster action scenes with shaky camera shots, Bri Larson's awkward acting, and a dull "I lost my memory. Who am I? Who are my friends and enemies?" predictable story, are all justified. Captain Marvel's smarm is more uncalled for, misplaced, or poorly delivered. As well, her characterization was minimal and you don't feel very invested in her story or motivations.

Samuel L. Jackson and pretty much every other actor gave a good performance, especially Carol's friend (I feel bad for not knowing her name, but they only said it maybe once or twice) because she showed a lot of emotion.

Overall, it was average and predictable. It had the quality of a Marvel movie, but lacked the Marvel charm. I'd give it a 6.5/10. Not bad, but not very good either.

title: What a meh movie
review:
Captain Marvel is the latest entry in the MCU, and it's certainly an interesting one. First off, I will say that Samuel L Jackson basically steals the show as Fury, he is both comedic and as legendary as he was in other movies.

Then we get to Carol herself and its just a string of "oh boy here we go"s. Carol's character in the movie is mainly snarky, a bit child-like, and extremely powerful for no real reason. This would all be fine if any of this actually lead to something, Tony Stark was the same way but still struggled against Stane, Whiplash, and even Thanos. You see Tony grow over the course of the films, going from lone wolf type of guy to someone who becomes a team player, and have that spirit crushed in Civil War. With Carol there is almost nothing. She doesn't really grow much as a character, with only highlights being when she finds out more about her past, and when she realizes what was actually taken from her. That is only one scene, and it is probably the quickest one in the entire movie. Plus her strength is never really tested, she doesn't seem to struggle at all. There is no final fight with the main villain, she just shoots him in the chest. Maybe this kind of stuff was supposed to be the comedic relief, but it's all hindered by Brie's performance. The entire time she almost seems like she didn't want to be there, most lines sound void of all personality. Now, when she was engaging in some banter with Fury or other cast members, Carol definitely became likeable, but those scenes weren't enough to salvage the movie.

Overall, 5/10. I feel like Carol's character can be redeemed in Endgame, and actually grow into a character that everyone can like.

title: MCU needs some tough love from us fans
review:
DISCLAIMER: This review is only relevant for those who have watched all MCU movies more than twice not because there was spare time but, just because... So, newbies... skiddadle!

Captain Marvel will make you sad. If you are a parent, it will make you feel the way it makes you sad when your child disappoints you; if you are an Arsenal fan, it's the way Ã–zil disappoints you; if you are an Mass Effect fan, it's the way Andromeda disappoints you; if you are an EU citizen, it is the way UK disappoints you or if you are an astronaut, it's the way Earth disappoints you... catch my drift?

The movie does not fail for Brie Larsson, neither for it's story line. It does because of hasty, careless impromptu development. Captain Marvel needed more time and as there lies the wasteland of the MCU newcomer.

Not to worry, I'll post my findings from its autopsy.

1. Absolute lack of character building. This is rampant through out the full run time, so much so that you'd never relate to the protagonist or the antagonist, EVER. Character base line is created with the laziest approach : flashback memory. The premise is that of a well-known trope that your Jane Doe is lost in the hapless C-35 looking for past identity. But the difference between this crap and Bourne Identity is that Jason Bourne is self conflicted at every step, whereas our cocky protagonist is super confident, to the point that she come of as arrogant! Viewers loved Iron Man (or Cap, or Natasha, or Dr. Strange, or Bucky, even Harbinger) because he suffered through hell to come out of the other end a changed man. A character arc is absolutely necessary for a origin story such as this one. It's like at points you'd almost want to get her ass handed to her which the movie never delivers.

2. Superbly clumsy writing. All the major plot points are told or narrated to you. They never unfold in front of your eyes. It's like the movie is always trying to tell you why you need to care about individual A or Plan B or side kick C. Major characters are never introduced with gravitas and never even mentioned why they are 'major' in the first place. More often than not the script becomes boring and monotonously child-like sci-fi extravagance. It's like watching Swat Cats on shrooms.

3. Typical MCU like abomination of a back ground score. The script tries too hard to deliver on the whole new trend of 90's nostalgia but fails miserably at best. Songs that are used are not well synchronized and does not go with the mood of the story line. You'll find yourself listening to a road-tripy kinda song when two major characters are driving trough a desert like road. That should work, right? BUT the movie forgets the fact that they are driving on a covert mission and one of them is having a continuous Dejavu! And rest assured that it never gets any better than that. It's so pathetic that at one point the movie had to invoke MCU's flag-ship title track... just to excite the viewer. Apart from this butchery of tracks the protagonist even often makes Aquaman-ish (Don't even get me started on this piece of crap) laughter enthused victory shrill during combat that'll makes one doubt if Hollywood would ever be able to portray a proper female superhero with dignity. (Yes, I hated Wonder woman too but that's a story for another time).

4. Humorless humor. Think about George Costanza in Seinfeld, Zoey Tribbiani in Friends or Phil Dunphy in Modern Family. They were funny and they made us believe that the actor playing the character is dumb and funny. Reason? Timing + Delivery. There are countably few good laughs in this movie but that's uncharacteristically forced. You'd get to see other 'naive' sides of pre-established MCU characters but the jokes very rarely work because of timing. Jokes are lipped by characters during stand offs, during situations when mistrust is dripping on the screen and sometimes it's just flat-out mistimed.

With all the anguish poured out I feel exhausted now. I expect more from MCU and may be it is not possible for a franchise this large to keep producing flicks that are unique and never sub-par. With Iron Man came a forgettable Hulk, With Avenger came a less than avg Age of Ultron, so after long spell of incredibly well-crafted origin stories like Back Panther, Dr. Strange, Spider Man and Ant Man, it is not entirely possible that our expectation of Captain Marvel was running feverishly high and it's a bit disappointing. After all that parent is proud of his/her child, the fan is glued to each Arsenal game, we are always replaying ME with fem Shepard, and the Astronaut comes back home. As for UK, our thoughts and prayers.

title: Better than expected
review:
I would just like to start this review off with a few things 1. I am not a fan of Brie Larson and the way she has acted in the past and during the lead up to this film's release 2. Please do not take every review you see as gospel, Disney are bribing critics for 100% positive reviews and that is something that should not be accepted. Heck, do not take my review as fact either. 3. I highly encourage people to see the movie for themselves before forming opinions and suggest leaving negativity about Brie Larson aside for at least 2 hours for this movie. 4. There are a lot of news outlets reporting on "trolls" leaving bad reviews on this film, and while yes trolls do leave bad reviews (they do on anything), there is a lot more to the whole situation that news outlets conviently leave out for the clicks and for the ad revenue.

Right now with that out of the way, I would like to start of by praising this film for several ressons 1. It went beyond my expectations 2. It was a nice way to tie up some loose ends in the MCU 3. It introduces us to more races in the MCU such as the Skrulls and Flurken (I am probably spelling that wrong) 4. It was great to see some more character development for Nick Fury 5. Talos was a very well done character and definitely the stand out character of the film 6. It was nice to see the Kree again after so long.

Now on to the bad: 1. Captain Marvel is portrayed as boring character, she seems bored most of the time, she has her moments but most of the time she is elevated by a much more enjoyable supporting cast. 2. The Kree are one dimensional, their motives boil down to, we want to conquer, you don't like it, tough. Once again they have their occasional moments but most of the time they feel like a generic army with no redeeming qualities writing wise.

To conclude, this movie isn't bad, but it isn't outstanding. Yes it was better than expected but that's mostly because I had my expectations set incredibly low (I did the same with Infinity War). I recommend giving this movie a shot, but it is not a must see.

Thank you for reading my review.

title: A decent movie that came out at the wrong time
review:
This movie has been making all kinds waves hasn't it, both good and bad but really to me all I care about is if I enjoyed it or not and i just have to say I enjoyed MOST of it.Captain Marvel was a good movie.

The critical point I can take away from this movie is that Brie Larsson as Captain Marvel was actually quite good, not amazing but she actually did a fine job as Captain Marvel, from the trailers she came off as dry and a charisma vacuum but thank goodness in the movie she was actually funny,witty and kind of charismatic for most of the movie like the usual Marvel Superheroes. She did however have some dry spells in the movie especially some of the dialogue but that didn't ruin the movie for me.So in short Brie Larson did a good enough job in the role of Captain Marvel.

The best characters by far where Yon-Rogg played by Jude Law and Talos the Skrull leader played by Ben Mendelsohn. Both gave very good performances and had compelling story arcs.While Samuel L Jackson as Nick Fury was good in the first and second act of the movie,and had great chemistry with Brie Larsson in the 3rd act of the movie Nick Fury become a chump and was rather useless in the movie although I get he is younger and not the Nick Fury we know from other Marvel movies he is just another different person in Captain Marvel which was kind of disappointing.Other characters such as Captain Marvel's friend Maria, the kree police force were fine or were just there and Phil Coulson and Roman were just glorified cameos.

What I liked about the movie was the the pace especially in the first and second act as the movie balanced action and story well.The movie had a fast pace but never too fast and I appreciateed that it didn't have the regular Origin Story formula, however I would have liked for the movie to explore more on Captain Marvel's origins so that I could Care about her character more as there isnt really much character development from Captain Marvel. Of course this is a Marvel movie so it had some funny moments and some uneeded and out of place humor as expected from a Marvel Movie. The skulls were really good in the movie especially Ben's performance as the Skrull leader Talos he was charismatic,funny and had an interesting arc. The movie takes an interesting twist involving the skrulls which was nice and made the movie more interesting.

The villain in this movie comes as a surprise in the movie so I won't spoil it but it is a good twist and makes sense so thumbs up for the villain with is rare for Marvel Movies.The action was fine, nothing spectacular but most of the action sequences were solid, they were just fine thats all I have to say about the action.The CGI was also very good especially the deaging process to Samuel L Jackson was very impressive and the effects on Captain Marvel's powers were cool especially when she had the helmet on it was bad ass.

Now by biggest issue with the movie and what I didn't enjoy was the 3rd act in this movie, my gosh especially the last 30 minutes were just disappointing. There were some bland action sequences,unfunny scenes and it was just the generic Marvel last third fight scene.Now one of the complaints from people is that the character of Captain Marvel is overpowered, I never count this as a bad thing if there are high stakes against the character and if the story is interesting. In Captain Marvel's case there was no serious threat in the 3rd act and the story became bland. Now the 3rd act wasn't that terrible but was just too generic and uninteresting and also really lazy.

Also speaking of lazy some of the dialogue was so cringey sometimes thankfully it was just a small bit but it was still noticeable and although I didn't want to speak on this the feminism and sjw aspect people are complaining about in Captain Marvel, I myself didn't care on those issues and although some of it is in the movie in sprinkles it wasnt preachy or anything as some people are exaggerating. It was noticeable but didn't make the movie bad.

Although I have to say in some scenes involving Captain Marvel especially scenes involving the past when she was being looked down appon,underestimated or bullied it was rather exaggerated and felt forced at times which made me cringe and didn't make me care about Brie Larsson's character at all.it was in small parts thankfully.

In terms of being Marvel's first female lead Superhero movie this was a fine(OK) attempt I guess.I mean this movie was mostly made to inspire little girls and look up to this character, you can say it did its job.

So Captain Marvel was a good movie,not a perfect movie at all and had a bland 3rd act the movie was still fun,funny and was mostly enjoyable.so am I excited to see Captain Marvel in Avengers: Endgame, no but i'm hopefull Marvel will improve this character and make her worth to watch and please if you haven't seen the movie go watch it for youself and come up with your own opinion.

title: A Stepping Stone Movie
review:
First of all: This movie will be enjoyable for great parts of the audience because it does contain scenes that are visually appealing, it does contain scenes that are comedic, and ensure laughter in the cinema, and it does contain scenes that are fun to watch. Even for someone like me, who wouldn't list this movie among Marvel's best, the movie did have enjoyable moments and I did go out of the cinema, knowing that I hadn't completely wasted my money.

One might say, that this movie contains everything other superhero movies do too. And to some extent I would agree with this statement, since it does contain fight scenes, scenes of emotion, and scenes of comedy. However the fight scenes consist of standard choreography, and cinematography and the scenes of nostalgia and emotion, because a tone that would provide for such scenes wasn't set, fail to be heartwarming. A theme of sisterhood, as it is present between Brie Larson's character and one of her past friends, doesn't work because the audience wasn't prepared for emotional depth due to the severe lack of character development, not just with Carol Denvers, but with most of the other characters. Therefore, scenes that are supposed to be heartwarming, seem generic and staged. I disagree with the argument that the lack of emotional depth is due to the great power that Carol has, since emotional depth doesn't always have to be created through external struggles, but can be created through internal struggles. However, because of the absence of complex character developments or arcs, the characters stay unbelievable and unrelatable while the incoherence of theme add on to the movie seeming as though it is unsure of what it wants to be. A character like Captain Marvel has to earn its place in the Marvel Universe. Characters such as Captain America or Iron Man earned their role over multiple films in multiple years. With this movie Marvel seems as though they want to force Captain Marvel into a position by simply saying: "Look how extremely powerful she is." which is non sensical, since it doesn't create bonds between the character and the audience. Something has yet to reasonably set up the character for a prime role in future Marvel movies.

Captain Marvel, for me, is nothing but a "filler" film which is supposed to lead on to other Marvel films featuring Captain Marvel. It is everything but concerned with character development or a coherent theme and therefore doesn't stand alone as a great story, but a product in the form of a story that had to be told in order to sell more stories in the future.

title: Below average for Marvel, but enjoyable.
review:
One problem for me is that I had recently seen Battle Angel Alita, which was what Captain Marvel could, and should, have been.
Another was that I had read the Captain Marvel and Ms. Marvel comics as a kid; way back in the 70s, and this movie version of Captain Marvel just didn't have the right attitude somehow. The movie version lost 50 IQ points, the hard-as-nails military attitude, and Brie Larsen's little girl voice in some scenes just didn't seem right.
In the Ms. Marvel comic series back in the 70s, she was an Air Force officer and chief of security at Cape Kennedy (Marvel Super-Heroes #13, March 1968). She got her powers in the same radioactive explosion that caused the original Captain Marvel to die of cancer. After resigning from the Air Force, she became a magazine editor who tackled issues like equal pay, equal rights, sexual harassment, etc. with J. Jonah Jameson as her favorite foil. The comic version was smart, fearless, and could make the tough decisions; in one issue of the comic, she let her best friend die in order to save hundreds of strangers. It looked like the movie version would have let them die to save her friend.
The comic version of Captain Marvel did a lot better job with the ending. In the comics, she tackled a young mutant named Rogue, who took her powers and sent her into a coma for 10+ years. That would have been a great ending for this movie. To wake up when Thanos snaps his fingers would have been a lot better than the ending we got.

title: A fun average Marvel film. I don't get all the hate

NOTE: I have been reading and watching tons of reviews and it seems that it all the reasons point out to something not related to the movie. Whether it's related to politics or feminism or whatever, we should always judge the movie on its own and not based on what Brie said about white critics (for example). I know this is a feminist movie, but personally, I thought the film wasn't shoving it into your face about it and that's why I at least found myself enjoying it and also I'm a dude. Brie Larson is okay as Carol Danvers. I do agree that she could've gave more emotion, but overall she was fine. I also noticed that her character doesn't go through too many struggles or challenges because she's so powerful and that bugged me a little. I can definitely see some room for improvement just like how I started loving Captain America and Thor a lot more in the first Avengers film. I'm expecting to see that kind of growth in Endgame for Captain Marvel.

I think my favourite scenes have to be the ones involving Nick Fury and Carol Danvers. They bring such a fun dynamic that I wanted more of it by the end of the film. The CGI is typical Marvel and it looks great. There's a certain song that plays at the end of the film and people think it was corny to put it in there, but at least it gave me the same vibe as when we heard "Immigrant Song" in Thor: Ragnarok.

Overall, I thought Captain Marvel was a fun, yet simple origin story that I welcome very well in the MCU!

I don't think it was Brie Larson's daily because she has proven to be a very alienated actress. Instead, I think it was the writing of the movie that just didn't quite get there for Carol Danvers.

title: Overall great 8/10
review:
After growing up in the 90s and with very little representation of female led superhero movies, I have to say that this movie has made the little girl in me quite happy.

The casting was great for the introduction of one of Marvel's toughest superheroes, especially with Brie Larson showcasing a witty, rough hero that has lost part of herself. Samuel L. Jackson, Goose, and the 90s nostalgia nailed perfectly the comedy parts of the movie without it being exaggerated.

As for the story, I think we still need to see Carol Danvers develop as a human a little more to be able to showcase her weaknesses so that she can complete her Hero's Journey and we can further empathize with her. Even as we learn about her past and how she acquired her powers, in my opinion her character feels a little unrealistically perfect.

On the other hand, the visual effects, action sequences and score were superb for this character's introduction. If you like rock music, you'll definitely enjoy a few sequences with Nirvana, No Doubt, and Garbage in the background.

Definitely a must see to keep up with the upcoming Avengers: Endgame.

Samuel Jackson - as usual steals the limelight despite being not the main character. Jude law is just appalling. Brie larson comes across as too uptight and doesn't strike as 'high in morale' as Captain America even if she is (in the comics).

Guest appearance by Ronan the accuser had me chuckling. (what a choice of a name )

It's worth one watch - not worth watching again.

title: Marvelous! ðŸ˜‰
review:
First of all, I will say I have a lot of feelings after watching this movie. I've been addicted to superhero movies ever since the first Iron Man movie came out when I was in second grade. Needless to say, I've grown up on superhero movies. However, this one was special - it's the first of the Marvel movies to have a female lead. Not that I don't love Black Widow, Scarlet Witch, or Zuri, but it's different having an actual female as the lead.

Anyway, it was a classic Marvel movie - the critical reviews surprise me. For reviewers calling Brie Larson "wooden" or "emotionless" - my interpretation was that it was a product of her childhood, adult life, and then finally Kree training. I grew up a tomboy, too - people constantly told me to grow up, to be less emotional, to stain my clothes less. Today, I've been told that people can't tell whether I'm happy or not or that I sound like Sadness from Inside Out. Carol Danvers is stiff and emotionless like this, too, especially after living as a Kree where she was TRAINED not to show emotions. I think when she finally broke free, she wasn't just free to use all of her powers - she was free to experience her emotions without caring what people thought.

Secondly, some people call Carol Danvers too powerful. This is a justified reason to critcize the movie, but I feel that this movie didn't fully flesh out what Carol can/can't do and we have more to look forward to in Avengers Endgame. What I can say is the scene where Carol smacked her fist and scared off Ronan was deeply satisfying. The fact that Captain Marvel is a woman and the (controversially!) most powerful Avenger makes me happy. Women can be strong and emotional! Women can be superheroes! I think these are the messages Marvel was trying to convey.

Thirdly, Goose. Goose is the reason everyone should watch this movie, and I laughed for about 5 minutes when I discovered Goose was the reason Fury got his scar.

Disregard the haters, PLEASE go see this awesome movie!

title: Went in with low expectation and was pleasantly surprised!
review:
After some of the reviews here you would think that this movie is a turd. I was close to canceling my tickets and skipping it but my kids still wanted to go. Consequently I went in with low expectations. You know what, I was pleasantly surprised! I found it an enjoyable use of two hours and I was engaged the entire time.

I'm not invested in Marvel comics but I have seen all the Marvel films. I watched it on how it stood up as a movie with no prior conceived notions as to what this character should be.

I see many complaints about the film being boring. I'm not sure what movie those reviewers saw. I found how Brie Larsen played Vers to be appropriate for what we discover her Kree background to be; "show no emotion". After she lands on Earth we see her begin to discover who she really is and who is really the enemy. I found the twist to be a surprise (for me) and the way it was handled well done.

Weaknesses? I can see the argument that Captain Marvel not having (an apparent) weakness to be something that may reduce the tension in the movie but our family never felt that. If you are someone that wants two hours of battle than perhaps you will be bored. But if you want more beyond a CGI-fest then I think there is a lot to be pleased about in this movie. Yes there are contrived conveniences but hey, it's a Marvel movie; they all have them. Is it logical? No. Is it fun, keeps you engaged for two hours? Yes. There have been other Marvel movies where I get bored with endless fights scenes (cough, cough Black Panther..) This one did not have that and for that I am thankful.

title: A decent but not great Marvel film...could learn a thing or two from Wonder Woman
review:
Casting aside all the backlash and controversy surrounding this movie I went to see it anyway before Infinity Wars Endgame comes out. It could've been better. Brie is a beautiful and talented actress but she was rather wooden and uncharismatic as Captain Marvel. I could never relate to or feel any attachment to her because she was so emotionless. Her one liner jokes really fell flat and barely anybody in the audience laughed. They tried too hard to make her as comedic as Robert Downy Jr.'s Tony Stark and it just didn't work. She never has the range of emotions that Gal Gadot's Wonder Woman did. From the joy of seeing a baby in a stroller to her first ice cream cone to her anguish and pain from Steve Trevor's sacrifice I identified and felt these emotions also. I didn't get that from Brie Larson's Captain Marvel.

Samue Jackson in his digital younger self was a hoot as was Goose the Cat. This kitty stole the show in my opinion. Carol Danvers memory flashbacks to introduce her origin were confusing at times. The writers were trying to cram too much background information in the first hour . It wasn't until well into the second half that things got interesting and the action picked up. Another big problem is that they wayOVER-powered her in this movie to be the Avenger's main weapon against Thanos in the upcoming Infinity Wars. No bad guy could even touch her in Captain Marvel. She holds off an entire fleet of Kree warships all by herself and has all of these awesome powers that she just only recently learned to control. Flash forward 25 years when Nick Fury sends her that distress signal and she's probably a thousand times more powerful. Thanos is pretty much toast.

I will say that the the two post credit scenes were good and almost worth the price of admission as was learning the hilarious and true reason why Nick Fury lost his eye and how the Avengers got their name. Do you need to see Captain Marvel before Infinity Wars...no. But if you have two hours and have nothing else to do it might be worth your time.
